candidates.title: Calibrate replay predictions against retained-order experiments
candidates.buyer: Multi-brand ecommerce teams and agencies deciding which Profound-generated changes deserve implementation.
candidates.problem: A simulated shopper can prefer an edited tool response even when production retrieval never sees it or real buyers do not purchase.
candidates.mechanism: Enabling stage: a calibrated selection rule redirects a fixed implementation budget toward interventions that cause more retained AI-origin orders. Simulation alone creates no purchases.
candidates.intervention: Build versioned, paired product-response replays with distinct consented buyer tasks, then join each predicted effect to a preregistered merchant experiment. Preserve retrieval source, model/version, timestamps, prompt family, product identity and uncertainty. Rank deployable changes by out-of-sample order evidence; quarantine rank-swaps as sensitivity tests.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Profound has live monitoring, a published crawler RCT and revenue attribution; DataFeedWatch already tests feed titles. A customer-facing purchase-calibrated replay release gate was not located in reviewed documentation. That gap is unverified, not a claim of absence.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Across held-out merchants and model versions, replay predictions select better purchase-producing changes than a factual-defect/frequency baseline at the same engineering budget.
dataNeeded: Consented distinct buyer tasks and hard constraints
Immutable control/treatment retrieval payloads and model versions
Randomized live deployment assignments and propagation dates
Merchant paid, canceled and refunded orders with stable origin instrumentation
candidates.experiment: First estimate transfer using randomized product-family clusters within merchants, keeping competing variants in one cluster. Then randomize matched merchant-category portfolios to replay-guided versus defect-priority selection at equal implementation hours. Primary endpoint is retained confirmed AI-origin orders per assigned portfolio over 12-16 weeks plus the return window. Power at portfolio level before starting; sparse order volume makes this a validation pilot. Keep all mandatory factual/safety corrections universal and record cross-category substitution.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat difference in retained AI-origin order counts per fixed portfolio-week, with clustered intervals; total retained merchant orders and net contribution are guardrails. Report simulation recommendation rates separately, never as shopper conversion. Unknown origins remain unknown.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase effect. markdown-rct documents causal testing of bot traffic only; gr0 provides adjacent attributed revenue, not an expected lift; function-calling establishes technical feasibility of a proxy.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured traffic or conversion baseline. Chosen monthly fee GBP 900, amortized implementation GBP 300 and net contribution GBP 30 per incremental retained order.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even = (900 + 300) / 30 = 40 additional retained orders per month versus the equal-budget selection baseline.
impactScenario.range: No predicted uplift range. Zero is plausible if replay adds no selection information; a negative result is plausible if it promotes persuasive but misleading changes.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP 900/month per multi-brand pilot, contingent on access to enough live experiment volume. Profound's custom Enterprise offer is a budget proxy, not proof of demand.
candidates.costControl: Reuse frozen retrieval payloads, test few orthogonal changes, and stop replaying stable failures. Preserve a small rotating holdout of new intents so caching does not hide model drift.
dependencies: Enough independent product clusters or portfolios
candidates.failureMode: Overfit simulations reward wording that performs only inside the custom tool; low volume or selection leakage creates false confidence.
candidates.falsifier: On a held-out live portfolio, replay-guided selection fails to improve retained orders over the cheaper baseline at equal implementation cost, or its predicted signs are no better than chance.

candidates.title: Carry consented shopping constraints into the exact cart
candidates.buyer: Merchants selling configurable products through their own shopping assistant or an approved AI shopping integration.
candidates.problem: A buyer selects a product for a specific size, budget and use case, then lands on a generic page and must reconstruct the decision.
candidates.mechanism: Handoff stage: preserving voluntarily supplied constraints and the chosen variant reduces reselection errors and repeat work, allowing more existing AI-origin buying intentions to become retained orders.
candidates.intervention: Create an expiring, opaque intent token in an integration we control. With buyer consent, it links a minimal constraint receipt to the selected variant, quantities and locale. Open a matching cart with a short fit summary and highlight any price or availability changes before checkout. Do not infer private chat content from a referrer.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify cart permalinks already preload variants and support attribution. OpenAI checkout integrations already carry transaction state. The proposed addition is consented constraint continuity and explicit mismatch resolution; access to native third-party conversations is not assumed.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Exact variant plus a visible explanation of preserved requirements produces more purchases than a plain preloaded cart, beyond the benefit of deep linking alone.
dataNeeded: Exact variant IDs and live pricing
Signed token lifecycle and consent records
Identical AI-origin tagging in both arms
candidates.experiment: Within the controlled shopping integration, randomize eligible shoppers before handoff to the same preloaded cart with or without the constraint receipt and mismatch UI. Keep each shopper in one assignment. Primary endpoint is retained paid orders within 14 days per randomized shopper. Run 6-8 weeks plus returns, or longer if the power calculation requires; test no automatic substitutions, unexpected charges or personal data in URLs.
candidates.metric: Retained paid-order rate = shoppers with at least one retained order / all randomized eligible shoppers. Estimate the treatment difference, including failed token opens. Measure exact-variant errors and total contribution alongside it.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. permalinks and acp document underlying handoff mechanisms; neither source supplies causal evidence for constraint receipts.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed traffic or order rate. Chosen fee GBP 300/month, amortized setup GBP 150/month, contribution GBP 30 per additional retained order.
impactScenario.calculation: (300 + 150) / 30 = 15 additional retained orders/month to cover these chosen costs.
impactScenario.range: No forecast. Effect can be zero if buyers already know the variant, or negative if the receipt adds friction or exposes stale assumptions.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot price: GBP 300/month for one storefront plus separately agreed setup. Test against a free plain-permalink implementation.
candidates.costControl: Store only short-lived references; use deterministic variant checks and existing cart APIs. Avoid an LLM call on every checkout.
dependencies: Controlled assistant or approved partner integration
candidates.failureMode: The extra explanation interrupts a ready buyer, or stale constraints select the wrong variant.
candidates.falsifier: Against the identical preloaded-cart control, the receipt does not improve retained-order rate or produces more variant-related returns.

candidates.title: Build complete compatible carts for task-based shoppers
candidates.buyer: Electronics, hobby, repair and home-office merchants whose customers need several interoperable components.
candidates.problem: AI recommends an attractive anchor product but leaves buyers unsure which cables, mounts, consumables or dimensions are necessary to complete their task.
candidates.mechanism: Selection-to-cart stage: a verified complete setup lowers unresolved compatibility uncertainty and prevents a buyer postponing the whole purchase. More items in existing orders alone does not satisfy the purchase objective.
candidates.intervention: Compile a merchant-reviewed compatibility graph and an executable task-to-cart solver. For a declared job and existing equipment, return the minimum complete set, optional additions clearly separated, incompatibilities, total delivered price and a stock-checked cart. Expose through an owned tool and crawlable configuration examples.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already provides bundles, related products and complementary quick-add. The proposed solver must verify required functional dependencies under buyer constraints rather than rebrand cross-selling or a fixed discounted kit.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Customers with unresolved setup requirements complete more orders when they can verify a whole working configuration, even without a bundle discount.
dataNeeded: Task-specific support contacts, return reasons and orders
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible AI-origin shoppers in the owned configurator to the existing complementary-product UI or the compatibility-checked task cart. Keep prices and discounts equal. Primary endpoint is retained paid orders per randomized shopper within 14 days; run 8-12 weeks plus returns, sized from the unresolved-task cohort. Guard against unnecessary accessories, false compatibility and a rise in total checkout price that depresses purchases.
candidates.metric: Difference in retained-order rate per all randomized eligible shoppers. Secondary metrics are complete-working-setup rate from voluntary follow-up, incompatibility returns and contribution; AOV is not counted as an extra purchase.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. bundles and recommendations establish substantial existing competition and integration primitives, not a measured effect of this solver.

impactScenario.baseline: No known purchase rate. Chosen monthly fee GBP 500, amortized setup GBP 250, contribution GBP 30 per incremental retained order.
impactScenario.calculation: (500 + 250) / 30 = 25 additional retained orders/month, excluding any AOV-only gain.
impactScenario.range: No forecast; zero or negative order impact is possible when larger carts overwhelm buyers or compatibility data is incomplete.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 500/month for one technically complex category, compared with native bundle and recommendation tools.
candidates.costControl: Cache approved compatibility edges and solve constraints deterministically. Reserve expert review for new models and conflicting specifications.
candidates.failureMode: Incomplete specifications falsely assure compatibility, or the minimum set is more expensive than buying elsewhere.
candidates.falsifier: Only basket size rises while the number of retained purchasing shoppers is unchanged, or incompatibility returns erase any order gain.

candidates.title: Route unmet brand demand to a verified seller with stock
candidates.buyer: Consumer brands distributed through multiple authorized retailers.
candidates.problem: An AI recommendation reaches an unavailable, wrong-market or misidentified offer while another authorized seller could fulfill the same product.
candidates.mechanism: Offer-selection stage: correctly linking the exact product to a feasible seller preserves otherwise lost brand demand. Moving an existing purchase from a retailer to DTC is channel redistribution, not incrementality.
candidates.intervention: Extend merchant observations into a permissioned product-and-seller identity graph: GTIN, model, pack size, region, seller authorization, warranty conditions, live stock and checkout links. Publish accurate seller facts to supported feeds and an owned purchase resolver. The resolver offers the buyer verified alternatives when the original offer cannot fulfill.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Profound already exposes the merchant layer; Shopify Catalog groups identical products; PriceSpider already provides retailer routing and availability. The edge must be agent-callable identity verification and measured recovery of unmet demand, not another where-to-buy widget.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A brand can recover more fulfilled purchases by resolving actual offer failures across retailers than by maximizing DTC checkout-link share.
dataNeeded: Retailer availability and allowed checkout links
Participating retailer order and return reports
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible unresolved-offer shoppers in the owned resolver to the existing retailer list or verified in-stock alternatives. Use identical disclosure and no paid ordering bias. Primary endpoint is retained brand purchases across participating sellers per randomized shopper within 14 days. Run 8-12 weeks plus returns after checking cross-retailer match coverage and power. Report missing retailer outcomes separately and guard against DTC cannibalization and extra travel/shipping burdens.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat difference in shoppers with a retained same-brand purchase / all randomized unresolved-offer shoppers. Deduplicate cross-retailer purchases where consent and data allow; otherwise bound the result rather than fabricate unique buyers.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. shopping, pricespider and shopify-mapping document adjacent capabilities; no direct measured incremental brand-order effect was found.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed failure prevalence or traffic. Chosen fee GBP 1,000/month, integration amortization GBP 500/month, brand contribution GBP 20 per additional sell-through order.
impactScenario.calculation: (1,000 + 500) / 20 = 75 incremental retained brand orders/month across participating retailers, not 75 shifted DTC orders.
impactScenario.range: No forecast. Net brand effect may be zero despite more tracked referrals; misrouting or stale stock can make it negative.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated brand pilot price: GBP 1,000/month plus integration, justified only if cross-retailer order access exists. Existing PriceSpider deployments are competition and potential integration partners.
candidates.costControl: Buy or integrate existing availability infrastructure. Refresh fast-selling or recently failed offers more often than stable long-tail products.
dependencies: Retailer data agreements and seller authorization evidence
candidates.failureMode: Retailers will not share order outcomes, stock is stale, or apparent gains merely reallocate existing brand sales.
candidates.falsifier: Total retained brand purchasing shoppers do not rise under complete reporting even though DTC share or resolver clicks increase.

candidates.title: Make delivery deadlines usable during AI product selection
candidates.buyer: Gift, event, travel and replacement-parts merchants with meaningful delivery urgency.
candidates.problem: A buyer's real requirement is arrival before a date; generic shipping text or stale AI summaries leave this unresolved until checkout.
candidates.mechanism: Discovery-to-checkout stage: a truthful, location-specific delivery estimate makes otherwise ambiguous products eligible for time-bound needs and reduces late checkout abandonment.
candidates.intervention: Expose a delivery-eligibility service in approved tools and merchant pages, using a buyer-supplied postcode and deadline. Return a timestamped estimate, order cutoff, shipping cost and honest confidence range, then revalidate at cart creation. Reuse the merchant's fulfillment system and invalidate affected promises when inventory or carrier conditions change.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Narvar already predicts delivery dates across PDP/cart/checkout and ACP carries fulfillment options. The proposed extension moves deadline qualification into the AI-origin selection flow and tests retained orders; prediction alone is not novel.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Providing the same accurate estimate before shortlist completion recovers more deadline-sensitive purchases than first revealing it at checkout.
dataNeeded: Merchant dispatch cutoffs and carrier estimates
Order-time quotes and actual delivery events
Orders, cancellations, returns and shipping subsidies
candidates.experiment: In an owned or approved shopping integration, randomize eligible deadline-sensitive shoppers before selection to early delivery qualification or the same estimate shown only at checkout. Primary endpoint is retained paid orders per shopper; predeclare on-time delivery as a critical guardrail. Run 6-10 weeks covering weekdays and peaks, plus delivery/return follow-up; size from the deadline cohort, not all traffic. Do not invent scarcity or overpromise dates.
candidates.metric: Retained-order rate per all randomized deadline-sensitive shoppers, with on-time retained orders and contribution after express-shipping costs reported separately. A more conservative estimate may lower raw orders while improving kept, on-time orders.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized for AI shopping. narvar supplies adjacent vendor conversion claims without a transferable effect size; acp supplies technical fulfillment fields.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured deadline demand or failure prevalence. Chosen fee GBP 500/month, integration GBP 250/month amortized, contribution GBP 25 per incremental retained on-time order after shipping.
impactScenario.calculation: (500 + 250) / 25 = 30 additional retained on-time orders/month.
impactScenario.range: No forecast. Zero is possible if deadlines are rare; negative contribution is possible if higher shipping costs or late deliveries exceed recovered orders.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot price: GBP 500/month, on top of any existing delivery-estimate provider. Test value against moving the merchant's current estimate earlier.
candidates.costControl: Integrate existing delivery providers, cache by origin/destination/service within a short validity window, and refresh on meaningful stock or carrier events.
dependencies: Approved tool or merchant-controlled entry flow
candidates.failureMode: Estimates are stale, cache geography is wrong, or early shipping costs discourage buyers.
candidates.falsifier: Early qualification does not increase retained on-time orders relative to showing the identical estimate at checkout, or late-delivery complaints increase.

candidates.title: Resolve obsolete AI recommendations to an explicit successor
candidates.buyer: Electronics, appliances and equipment brands with annual models or discontinued products that still appear in AI recommendations.
candidates.problem: Old comparisons and product identities send buyers to a discontinued model, while the current replacement's differences remain unclear.
candidates.mechanism: Discovery-to-selection stage: preserving the old model's identity and presenting a verified successor lets buyers complete a relevant purchase instead of hitting a dead end. Substitution requires the buyer's agreement.
candidates.intervention: Build a versioned model-lineage graph from manufacturer records. Add visible predecessor/successor pages with exact differences, retained/lost compatibility, price changes and stock. Resolve an old model to a choice between remaining stock and a supported successor in owned tools; update supported feeds without reusing old item IDs.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Schema.org already represents ProductModel successors, and ordinary ecommerce redirects/product recommendations handle replacements. Profound FactCheck detects outdated claims. The proposed value is verified lineage plus explicit difference-aware choice and a live order test, not adding schema alone.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A precise successor comparison converts more high-intent visits from obsolete AI recommendations than a generic redirect or generic related-product list.
dataNeeded: Old-model AI referral and owned-tool events
candidates.experiment: Randomize AI-origin visitors arriving at known obsolete-model pages before rendering to the existing discontinued-product experience or the successor comparison. Keep every arm truthful and preserve required safety/recall information. Primary endpoint is retained paid orders per visitor within 30 days. Run 8-12 weeks plus returns; cluster returning users and power from obsolete-model traffic. Measure all replacement purchases, not only the featured successor.
candidates.metric: Retained-order rate per randomized obsolete-model entrant and model-confusion return rate. Public feed/lineage publication, if separately tested, needs randomized model families and fixed family-week order counts because it can change incoming traffic.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. successor establishes a representation, factcheck establishes adjacent diagnostics, and openai-feed establishes stable identity requirements; none proves conversion improvement.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed obsolete-referral volume. Chosen fee GBP 250/month, amortized curation GBP 100/month, contribution GBP 35 per additional retained order.
impactScenario.calculation: (250 + 100) / 35 = 10 incremental retained orders/month.
impactScenario.range: No forecast. Zero is plausible when legacy demand is tiny; negative effects arise when a successor loses a feature that made the original relevant.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated price: GBP 250/month per frequently refreshed product family portfolio, with setup charged against measured lineage complexity.
candidates.costControl: Review only actual model changes and observed legacy demand. Use deterministic ID joins after a human approves ambiguous lineage.
dependencies: Merchant control of obsolete product pages
Persistent shopper assignment and order tracking
Human review of material product differences
candidates.failureMode: A related product is mistaken for a true successor, or the replacement no longer satisfies the original task.
candidates.falsifier: The experience produces no retained-order gain over truthful existing replacement pages, or wrong-model returns offset the gain.

candidates.title: Show an evidence-backed fit verdict for an unfamiliar product
candidates.buyer: Challenger brands whose products appear in AI shortlists but face buyer uncertainty at the first merchant visit.
candidates.problem: An AI-generated 'best for' label gives the buyer a reason to look, but the merchant page often cannot verify the exact benefit or explain the tradeoff.
candidates.mechanism: Evaluation stage: a short, checkable fit verdict reduces justified uncertainty and helps a suitable buyer decide. It should also steer unsuitable buyers away, limiting regret and returns.
candidates.intervention: Create a compact decision component from verified product tests and specifications: meets, does not meet, and unknown for buyer-selected requirements, with evidence links and a plainly stated downside. Use the same facts in readable comparison pages. Compare real alternatives fairly and avoid invented reviews or claims about why a private AI chat chose the product.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Profound already has FactCheck and comparison-content workflows. The proposed intervention is a shopper-controlled fit decision with honest unknowns, tested against the existing PDP; evidence links alone are not a differentiated business.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: For unfamiliar products with a clear use-case match, verifiable tradeoffs increase retained orders more than generic persuasive copy and reduce fit-related returns.
dataNeeded: Orders, return reasons and support questions
candidates.experiment: Randomize identified AI-origin PDP entrants to the current page or the fit component, with assignment before requirement entry. Keep mandatory disclosures in both. Primary endpoint is retained paid orders within 14 days per randomized entrant. Run 6-8 weeks plus returns, powered for the unfamiliar-product cohort; analyze users who decline the component as assigned. Guard against false reassurance and artificially negative competitor descriptions.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat retained-order-rate difference per all randomized AI-origin entrants. Report fit-related returns and contribution, and distinguish comprehension improvement from a purchase effect.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase impact. shortlist supplies adjacent observations about comparative decision behavior, not sales causality; factcheck documents substantial existing overlap.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed AI traffic or baseline conversion. Chosen fee GBP 250/month, evidence review GBP 100/month, contribution GBP 35 per additional retained order.
impactScenario.calculation: (250 + 100) / 35 = 10 additional retained orders/month; returns must already be deducted from contribution.
impactScenario.range: No forecast. The component can have zero effect or reduce orders by introducing friction; fewer unsuitable purchases may improve returns without increasing purchases.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 250/month for one category, compared with a merchant-written fit table and existing CRO tooling.
candidates.costControl: Use deterministic requirement matching for approved facts; update only affected evidence when the product or test record changes.
candidates.failureMode: The component becomes another marketing badge, adds cognitive work, or falsely resolves unknown requirements.
candidates.falsifier: Only engagement or confidence rises, while retained-order rate and net contribution do not improve against a simple factual table.

candidates.title: Attach the correct helmet-standard evidence to the exact product
candidates.buyer: US adult bicycle-helmet brands and authorized specialist retailers with complete product testing records.
candidates.problem: A buyer or assistant cannot confidently distinguish a bicycle helmet's actual standard, use limits and manufacturing identity from generic safety language or a similarly named variant.
candidates.mechanism: Requirement qualification stage: accessible, correctly scoped evidence helps genuinely suitable products survive hard-filter shopping and reduces uncertainty before purchase. Documentation never makes an unsuitable or recalled product safe.
candidates.intervention: Build a supplier-reviewed evidence dossier linked to model, intended use, production identification and applicable manufacturer/importer certification records. Publish accurate, human-readable claims and source links on the PDP and approved tool output. Return unknown when identity or evidence does not match; never label a product 'CPSC approved' based on our software.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Profound FactCheck already compares claims with a source of truth. Suppliers already maintain compliance information. The extension is exact-product applicability and buyer-accessible evidence, not automated legal certification or a generic accuracy score.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: For shoppers explicitly requiring a US bicycle standard, precise supporting evidence increases retained suitable-product purchases over equally compliant pages with only the existing standard statement.
dataNeeded: Current product status and safety notices
candidates.experiment: All mandatory warnings, required labels, recall actions and factual corrections remain in both arms. Randomize eligible AI-origin adult-helmet shoppers to standard compliant PDPs or those pages plus the optional evidence dossier. Primary endpoint is retained paid orders per randomized shopper within 14 days. Run 8-12 weeks plus returns, sized from this narrow cohort. Stop for any incorrect applicability or misleading safety claim; no experiment withholds necessary safety information.
candidates.metric: Retained-order-rate difference among all randomized shoppers in the predeclared standard-seeking cohort. Track evidence errors, wrong-use purchases and complaints as critical guardrails; do not treat a certificate download as conversion.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized commercial effect. cpsc verifies the regulatory context and documentation requirements as checked September 29, 2026. It does not endorse this service or establish that an evidence display increases sales.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured standards-led traffic or conversion. Chosen fee GBP 750/month, specialist review GBP 250/month, contribution GBP 25 per incremental retained order.
impactScenario.calculation: (750 + 250) / 25 = 40 incremental retained orders/month to cover the chosen service and review costs.
impactScenario.range: No sales forecast. Zero is plausible if the existing label is sufficient; negative impact is possible from confusion or slow evidence review.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot price: GBP 750/month for a specialist category. Price must include qualified supplier review; do not charge for a claimed compliance guarantee.
candidates.costControl: Reuse approved evidence across genuinely identical models and lots while keeping applicability explicit. Avoid generating new legal interpretations with each request.
dependencies: Current official requirements and product status
candidates.failureMode: A model-level document is wrongly applied to a different product, or shoppers mistake the display for regulator endorsement.
candidates.falsifier: Correctly matched dossiers produce no retained-order gain against a compliant control, or applicability errors cannot be kept at zero.

candidates.title: Recover valid AI-origin checkout sessions after a handoff error
candidates.buyer: Merchants with approved agentic checkout or owned assistant-to-store integrations.
candidates.problem: A chosen product can fail at checkout because the quoted state expired, a region is unsupported, authentication is needed or a recoverable message is not actionable.
candidates.mechanism: Checkout stage: identifying the exact recoverable condition and returning the buyer to an authoritative existing session can rescue genuine buying intent without duplicating charges or silently changing the order.
candidates.intervention: Build a checkout adapter and conformance suite that compares discovery offers with current merchant state, preserves session identity, translates structured errors into one clear correction, and provides a safe merchant-checkout fallback. Require explicit acceptance of changed price, item or fulfillment. Keep payment handling in the merchant's existing system.
candidates.competitorOverlap: ACP already defines authoritative checkout state, structured errors and retry keys; Shopify already supplies cart links. The product is a tested merchant adapter plus recovery UX and order evidence, not invention of those protocol features. Access is partner-dependent.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A merchant-specific adapter recovers more retained orders than current generic error handling among valid sessions with remediable faults.
dataNeeded: Payment/order confirmations, refunds and duplicate-charge reports
candidates.experiment: Test protocol correctness in a merchant sandbox first. For live recoverable errors, randomize shopper sessions before displaying either existing safe error handling or the improved correction/fallback. Both arms retain essential retry safety and required disclosures. Primary endpoint is retained paid orders within seven days per randomized error session. Run 8-12 weeks plus returns or longer if faults are rare; reject any duplicate charge, unauthorized substitution or consent regression.

candidates.title: Offer a real, short stock hold after an explicit buyer choice
candidates.buyer: Merchant with measured stock races between assistant recommendation and checkout
candidates.problem: A shopper may decide on an available item in an assistant and lose it during handoff. Repeating discovery can lose the purchase.
candidates.mechanism: Availability continuity: a buyer-requested, time-limited reservation keeps a confirmed choice available through checkout. The gain must exceed displaced purchases from other shoppers; scarce inventory cannot be counted twice.
candidates.intervention: In a cooperating shopping flow, offer a clearly labeled short reservation only after the shopper selects the item. Integrate a supported inventory-hold mechanism, publish the actual expiry, cap holds per buyer/session, release promptly and honor ordinary checkout confirmation. Never reserve merely because a bot retrieved a listing.

candidates.experiment: Randomize inventory pools or SKU-by-time blocks to optional holds or the existing no-hold flow, with washout longer than maximum hold duration. Primary endpoint is total retained purchases per inventory-pool-hour; identifiable AI-origin retained orders are a subgroup endpoint. Do not randomize individual users sharing the same scarce stock without modeling interference. Run several replenishment cycles; guardrails: other-channel conversion, capacity lockup and fraud.
candidates.metric: Total retained orders per assigned pool-hour at comparable stock availability, plus AI-origin retained orders and reservation expiry. A rise in AI orders with an equal fall elsewhere fails the incremental-purchase objective.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. shopify-reservation establishes an available reservation mechanism, not demand or a measured sales effect; openai-shopping establishes that commerce information can lag.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown stock-race frequency, available units, replenishment rate, hold acceptance and displaced demand.

impactScenario.range: No numerical range; zero under fixed inventory sold out either way, negative if reservations block more real buyers than they help.

candidates.failureMode: Holds create artificial shortages, enable abuse or shift purchases without adding any.
candidates.falsifier: Storewide retained orders fail to increase despite higher AI-origin orders, or hold abuse/displacement consumes the benefit.

candidates.title: Resume a failed agent checkout without losing the chosen cart

candidates.problem: Agent checkout can encounter a buyer-review requirement, expired state or an uncertain payment response. Losing the chosen cart or retrying blindly can destroy a ready purchase.
candidates.mechanism: Checkout completion: a deterministic recovery path preserves valid choices, resolves whether an order already exists and hands the buyer to the merchant for required review. It can rescue a purchase while avoiding duplicate orders or unwanted charges.
candidates.intervention: Build a conformance and recovery adapter around supported checkout status APIs. On eligible failure, retrieve authoritative state, use the business-provided continuation URL, show material changes for buyer confirmation and resume using correct idempotency. Test failure cases with replayed tool responses before any live cohort; reconcile final merchant receipts.

The opportunity is tested implementation quality across real connectors and purchase outcomes. candidates.edgeHypothesis: For merchants with observed recoverable handoff failures, a correct, low-friction implementation produces more retained purchases than the current standards-compliant continuation flow.
dataNeeded: Connector checkout states and versioned error taxonomy
Cart and quote hashes without payment credentials
Idempotency keys and authoritative order status

candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. ucp-checkout and shopify-carts document the existing technical baseline; no reviewed source measures this adapter's incremental AI purchases.

candidates.title: Attach an executable compatibility witness to each recommendation
candidates.buyer: A parts, accessories or equipment merchant where buyers need an exact technical match.
candidates.problem: Readable product facts still leave buyers uncertain whether an item works with the exact device, version or setup they own.

candidates.intervention: Compile manufacturer compatibility tables, dimensions and exclusions into versioned predicates. Given a buyer-supplied model/version, return supported, unsupported or unknown, with the source and rule used. Guardrails: wrong-fit returns, false-compatible verdicts and escalation for unknowns; hazardous categories require expert-validated rules before participation.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based pilot: USD500/store/month for one category with licensed data; validate against the merchant's existing fitment supplier and quiz tools.
candidates.costControl: Evaluate compiled rules deterministically and reserve model calls for extracting questions or routing unknowns. Do not lower the evidence threshold to reduce maintenance.
candidates.failureMode: Identifier ambiguity or stale source tables silently produce false compatibility; many categories lack maintainable ground truth.
candidates.falsifier: No increase in retained compatible orders versus the existing tool, or the false-compatible rate exceeds the preregistered safety threshold.

candidates.title: Offer a real short inventory hold during the AI handoff
candidates.buyer: A merchant with genuine stock races during multi-step AI-assisted purchases and inventory that is not predictably sold out regardless.
candidates.problem: Availability can change while a shopper moves from a valid recommendation through clarification and payment, causing failed purchases.
candidates.mechanism: A real, brief merchant-backed reservation can keep the selected item available while the buyer completes a chosen checkout. It creates incremental purchases only if rescued orders exceed displaced purchases elsewhere.
candidates.intervention: Integrate an explicit buyer-requested reservation with expiration, release and abuse limits. Use a supported inventory or draft-order reservation path, verify compatibility with the intended checkout, and show truthful hold status. Do not simulate scarcity, reserve on crawler traffic, or treat an ordinary cart as a stock hold.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify's DraftOrderInput already supports reserveInventoryUntil. The work is an agent handoff policy, checkout compatibility and an all-channel incrementality test; reservation as a primitive is not novel.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: For catalogs with recoverable stock races and spare aggregate supply, properly limited holds increase completed AI-origin orders without reducing total purchases across the shared inventory pool.
dataNeeded: Inventory pool and concurrent demand history
candidates.experiment: Randomize whole disjoint inventory pools or SKU-by-time blocks to holds enabled versus existing availability rechecks, with blocks longer than hold duration and a release washout. Primary endpoint: paid AI-origin orders per assigned pool-day, with a required no-harm and incremental check on total paid orders across the same pool. Run through multiple restock cycles and a cluster-power plan. Guardrails: non-AI conversion, hoarding, hold abuse, expired inventory and payment failures.
candidates.metric: Count paid orders across the full shared inventory pool, not merely reservation users. Report AI-origin order gains alongside all-channel order changes; channel substitution alone is not an incremental-purchase success.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. shop-reserve supports technical feasibility of one reservation primitive; shop-cart documents agent checkout options. Neither supplies evidence for the proposed reservation policy's net purchase effect.

impactScenario.baseline: Assume USD300/month and USD40 contribution per genuinely additional retained order; inventory is not assumed plentiful and must be audited.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even = 300 / 40 = 7.5, rounded to eight additional retained orders/month, after subtracting displaced orders and operating costs.
impactScenario.range: Zero if all units would sell anyway, making this only a timing or channel shift; negative if holds block more ready buyers than they rescue.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based pilot: USD300/store/month only after measuring stock-race losses and excluding always-sold-out inventory pools.
candidates.costControl: Create holds only after explicit high-intent requests and expire them automatically. Avoid running a costly model to decide stock ownership.
candidates.failureMode: Holds merely redistribute scarce inventory, obstruct other buyers or break native checkout features.
candidates.falsifier: AI-source completion rises but total inventory-pool purchases do not, or displaced sales and operational cost erase the gain.

candidates.title: Carry a verified item decision from AI selection into the final cart
candidates.buyer: Merchants with multiple size, pack, condition or market variants

candidates.title: Resolve ambiguous fitment before recommending a part
candidates.buyer: Automotive parts and other compatibility-sensitive merchants.
candidates.problem: A part appears relevant to a model name but fails on an engine, trim or production-year qualifier, or the shopper abandons because compatibility remains uncertain.

candidates.title: Reconcile buyer entitlements across a distributor network
candidates.buyer: Manufacturers and distributors selling through multiple regional or specialist dealers.
candidates.problem: An authenticated business buyer can have valid contract terms at several dealers, but an AI shopping journey compares public prices and loses approved quantities or purchasing authority at each handoff.
candidates.mechanism: Discovery-to-purchase stage: with explicit account linking, compare the buyer's genuinely available offers and prepare a permitted purchase, reducing repeated authentication and quote reconstruction.
candidates.intervention: Build adapters that read scoped dealer entitlements, pack units, available terms and approval requirements, then prepare a common requisition with dealer-specific checkout links. Every supplier validates its own price and permissions; human approval remains where required.
candidates.competitorOverlap: UCP already defines consented identity linking; BigCommerce MCP already supports B2B lists, approvals, quotes and checkout. Feedonomics already distributes customized partner data. The candidate increment is reconciliation across heterogeneous authorized dealer systems, not single-store B2B chat.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A shared comparison and requisition can convert more qualified AI-origin procurement requests across the distribution network than separate existing portals.
candidates.experiment: Randomize consenting buyer-company accounts, not sessions, to existing dealer workflows or the cross-dealer adapter for 8-16 weeks subject to B2B sales-cycle power. Primary endpoint: completed paid and fulfilled orders per eligible procurement request across the network. Guard unauthorized disclosure, price errors, supplier displacement and approval bypass; measure total network purchases.
candidates.metric: Retained fulfilled orders / all pre-registered eligible procurement requests from randomized companies. Dealer share shifts without a network purchase gain are not incremental conversion.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. ucp-identity and b2b-mcp document substantial native overlap; ace and platform support distribution integration feasibility, not cross-dealer purchase lift.

impactScenario.baseline: No assumed eligible request volume. Chosen monthly fee USD 3,000 plus amortized integration/support USD 2,000; contribution per incremental fulfilled order USD 200.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even = (3,000 + 2,000) / 200 = 25 additional fulfilled orders/month across the paying network.
impactScenario.range: Zero if portals already work well; negative if account-linking friction, stale terms or integration support consume the benefit.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated network-level pilot: USD 3,000/month plus explicitly scoped implementation. Individual dealers may not pay for a tool that redistributes their existing orders.
candidates.costControl: Start with two systems and a common entitlement model; cost permission maintenance and support as service labor, not negligible software overhead.
candidates.failureMode: Suppliers refuse comparisons, entitled prices cannot be retrieved safely, or reconciliation duplicates an existing procurement suite.
candidates.falsifier: Buyers gain convenience but network orders do not rise, or the adapters cannot preserve permissions and accurate terms.

candidates.title: Turn a consented owned-product record into a timely reorder
candidates.buyer: Merchants selling non-medical consumables and replacement parts with recurring need.
candidates.problem: A previous AI-assisted purchase solves a one-off search, but the shopper later has to reconstruct the exact model, compatible consumable and preferred quantity.
candidates.mechanism: Repeat-purchase stage: retain a minimal, consented ownership record and buyer-chosen review date; a supported assistant can later present a current compatible reorder with less search effort.

candidates.metric: Retained repeat orders / randomized opted-in accounts across the whole observation window. Report AI-origin repeat sessions separately; do not count an earlier purchase as an incremental later purchase.

candidates.title: Buy the missing product facts that block real shopper decisions
candidates.buyer: Managed-feed teams and merchants whose products lack decision-critical source facts.
candidates.problem: Enrichment can restate available facts, but cannot truthfully answer a hard requirement absent from every source, such as a measured internal dimension or a tested compatibility exception.
candidates.mechanism: Understanding-to-selection stage: allocate a fixed expert/supplier effort budget to obtaining genuinely missing facts that prevent qualified shoppers from buying. Cost control matters only if the acquired facts create additional retained purchases.
candidates.intervention: Group consented unanswered shopping requirements by product family, verify the source gap, estimate affected demand without inventing uplift, and commission the smallest supplier confirmation or physical measurement. Store the result and scope before publishing; compare its purchase effect with usual manager-selected work.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Feedonomics already integrates supplemental data, works with dedicated managers and refuses unsupported enrichment facts. A generic extraction or approval queue is not the idea. The candidate edge is an explicit value-of-information budget for acquiring new evidence with purchase-based follow-up.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Demand-weighted fact acquisition creates more retained purchases per fixed expert-hour than catalog-wide completeness targets.
dataNeeded: Source inventories and actual evidence gaps
candidates.experiment: Randomize matched product families with verified missing facts to immediate evidence acquisition or the merchant's normal backlog at equal total expert hours. Primary endpoint: retained purchases per family-week, with AI-origin orders separately identified. Use 8-12 weeks if powered and allow ingestion/return maturity; never fabricate a value for control products or delay a safety-critical correction.
candidates.metric: Incremental retained orders per randomized family-week; secondary efficiency is additional retained orders per expert-hour and total delivered cost. Completion percentage is not the objective.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. source-data, service and euro establish the source dependency and managed labor already involved; they do not establish the proposed prioritizer's advantage.

impactScenario.baseline: No assumed missing-fact prevalence or buyer demand. Chosen monthly software fee USD 1,000 plus supplier/measurement labor USD 1,000; contribution USD 40 per retained order.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even = (1,000 + 1,000) / 40 = 50 additional retained orders/month attributable to the new evidence.
impactScenario.range: Zero if missing facts are not purchase blockers; negative if collection is expensive, slow, wrong or distracts from better work.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot: USD 1,000/month plus a capped, fully disclosed evidence-collection budget.
candidates.costControl: Reuse a verified family-level measurement only where physically valid; stop buying evidence when the next fact's likely value cannot justify its full acquisition cost.
dependencies: Permission to collect and publish facts
candidates.failureMode: Questions reflect curiosity rather than demand, one measurement does not generalize to variants, or vendor response time makes the facts arrive too late.
candidates.falsifier: At equal expert hours, acquired facts improve completeness but not retained purchases versus the existing managed-service backlog.

candidates.intervention: Record source-field and supplier-revision dependencies for generated facts. On a material edit, invalidate only affected facts, obtain merchant-approved replacement facts and publish them through the correct route: Merchant Center for Google or Shopify sources for Catalog. candidates.title: Quote the payable offer for the actual destination before cart abandonment
candidates.buyer: Cross-border merchants whose product price is attractive but delivery fees, minimum spend or local pricing change the decision.
candidates.problem: The AI-visible item price can fit a budget while the order available to this shopper does not; uncertainty or a late surprise then destroys the purchase.
candidates.mechanism: Selection and checkout: an early, honest estimate can identify a feasible service, quantity or alternative before commitment. It may reduce unsuitable checkouts while increasing completed, kept purchases among shoppers with a feasible offer.
candidates.intervention: Use the shopper's chosen destination and exact variant/quantity to obtain a Shopify cart estimate, including applicable discounts and available delivery choices. State which taxes or duties remain unresolved, timestamp the quote and reconcile it at checkout. Offer optional feasible alternatives; never promise an estimate is final.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already exposes buyer-aware cart costs; Simprosys already submits Markets feeds, promotions and Google automated discounts. Another price field or coupon engine is insufficient differentiation.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Joining the published AI offer to the merchant's payable cart catches economically consequential discrepancies that separate feed and checkout tools do not explain.

Compare current localized page with the quote workflow for 6-8 weeks plus refund maturation, sized from actual cross-border volume. Primary endpoint: kept purchases per assigned visitor. Guard page latency, margin, estimate error and privacy friction.
candidates.metric: Intent-to-treat kept-order probability among prequalified arrivals; quote acceptance and checkout starts remain diagnostics. Contribution after fulfilment is a guardrail.

candidates.mechanism: Discovery and comparison: correct product identity can place an offer in the right comparison set and make a fair unit-price assessment possible. The purchase effect requires that erroneous identity was actually excluding or misleading prospective buyers.
candidates.intervention: Build a merchant-reviewed identity record linking supplier evidence, GTIN/MPN, pack composition, condition and seller role. Reconcile source feeds, rendered pages and allowed Catalog mappings; distinguish a manufacturer bundle from a merchant-created kit. candidates.title: Check that each AI checkout route can fulfil the actual product requirements
candidates.buyer: Merchants with required custom inputs, checkout apps, bundles or fulfilment options that differ across channels.
candidates.problem: A valid product feed does not guarantee that the selected AI checkout can collect the required information or offer the necessary fulfilment method.
candidates.mechanism: Checkout completion: identifying route incompatibility before exposure and moving supported validation to server logic can prevent dead-end or invalid orders. A supported merchant checkout can preserve sales when an embedded route cannot meet requirements.
candidates.intervention: Inventory required product and checkout capabilities, compare them with each channel's current contract, and replay approved sandbox carts through the supported path. Primary endpoint: kept AI-origin orders per randomized store-week, adjusted for pre-period levels. Guard all-channel orders, loss of useful direct checkout, unsupported item sales and checkout latency.
candidates.metric: Difference in kept AI-origin orders per assigned store-week; keep unsupported-product exposure and invalid orders as diagnostics. Use Shopify order records rather than relying only on storefront pixels.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. Shopify documents real capability and pixel limitations (google-ai); no evidence establishes their prevalence or incremental revenue under this proposed repair process.

impactScenario.range: Negative if fallback loses the benefits of a working direct checkout; zero if native support already handles every important requirement.

candidates.title: Recover the shopping intent behind a dead product link
candidates.buyer: Shopify merchants with discontinued, renamed or seasonally replaced products and measurable AI referrals.
candidates.problem: Stage: landing recovery. An assistant can cite an old product URL. A generic homepage redirect discards the product requirements and makes the visitor restart.
candidates.mechanism: Remember the retired item's verified constraints, offer an honest replacement choice, and reduce the work needed to reach a suitable purchasable item. Orders increase only if compatible inventory exists and the failed-link cohort is large enough.
candidates.intervention: Create a merchant-approved replacement map using retired product snapshots, current stock and hard compatibility rules. Show a fast discontinuation/replacement page with the old item's identity, two qualified alternatives and explicit differences; retain a normal failure page when no fit exists.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Smart SEO already detects 404s and supports custom and automated redirects. Its documented manual Fix defaults to the homepage. The proposed difference is tested preservation of buying constraints; absence of this precise workflow elsewhere is not established.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A constraint-preserving recovery page beats both the merchant's current redirect and a competent manually chosen replacement, rather than merely beating a broken page.
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible arriving human sessions, sticky by visitor, between current relevant redirect and recovery page. Primary: at least one paid order within 7 days per assigned session. Run 8 weeks after a baseline power check; extend recruitment if faults are rare. Track returns through the merchant return window, redirect loops, latency and unrelated-product complaints.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat difference in 7-day purchaser rate among all preclassified eligible AI arrivals, including people who never click an alternative. Report the source-detection coverage and all-channel result separately; orders are counted once.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; smartseo-links documents the recoverable workflow, not its sales effect.

candidates.title: Keep the chosen variant and market intact from answer to cart
candidates.buyer: Multi-variant, multi-market Shopify stores whose referred shoppers must reselect size, model or currency.
candidates.problem: Stage: arrival to checkout. A recommendation for one purchasable variant can land on a default variant or a different market's offer, even when catalogue grouping is correct.
candidates.mechanism: Preserve explicit item/variant/market selections, revalidate current price and stock, and explain any change before adding to cart. This can prevent reselection errors and offer surprises that interrupt an otherwise viable purchase.

candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; shipperhq-date establishes an existing operational engine, not purchase gain from moving it upstream.

candidates.title: Make compatibility answers fail closed on unknown facts
candidates.buyer: Electronics accessories, replacement-parts and equipment merchants where one wrong specification invalidates the purchase.
candidates.problem: Stage: understanding and qualification. A fluent product description can leave an assistant unable to distinguish compatible, incompatible and unknown configurations.
candidates.mechanism: Source-backed hard constraints prevent false recommendations while allowing truly compatible products to be selected with confidence. Purchases should rise among qualified needs and wrong-fit returns should fall; fewer recommendations overall can be healthy.
candidates.intervention: Build an auditable compatibility graph from manufacturer documents and merchant-verified tests, including explicit exclusions, version boundaries and unknown states. candidates.title: Choose a valid purchase route before a cart hits an unsupported checkout
candidates.buyer: Merchants with customizable products, pickup needs or checkout applications, and shopping-agent developers who control the referral interface.
candidates.problem: A recommended product can require capabilities that a direct AI checkout cannot provide. Native fallback exists, but the buyer can still encounter an unsuitable route before discovering that limitation.
candidates.mechanism: Stage: checkout completion. Detecting the actual cart's requirements before routing it should reduce repeated forms, missing options and abandoned handoffs while retaining valid orders.
candidates.intervention: Build a tested capability manifest for each merchant, cart type and channel. An authorized agent chooses an allowed direct checkout or a prefilled storefront handoff, explains any required action, and preserves the selected variant and attribution. Do not change third-party routing without a supported integration.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already provides continuation URLs, escalation and preserved-cart fallback; Google/Copilot support some blocking extensions. The proposed edge is proactive merchant-specific conformance and route evaluation, not inventing fallback.

Primary endpoint: at least one paid order per assigned mission within 7 days. Run at least 4 weeks and power on the affected-cart subgroup; do not count repeat attempts as independent buyers. Guard against validation bypass, extra latency, returns and channel substitution.
candidates.metric: Paid purchasing missions / all randomized eligible missions, including missions that never reach checkout. Report missing-configuration errors separately.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. google, copilot, meta and cart-checkout document constraints and fallback, not how often failures occur or a measured recovery rate.

impactScenario.baseline: Let N be eligible AI missions, f the measured share encountering route mismatch and r the net purchase recovery among that share.
impactScenario.calculation: Potential added paid missions = N*f*r, before subtracting failures caused by additional routing. Measure f and r; neither is supplied here.
impactScenario.range: No evidence-based lift range. Zero or negative effects remain possible; estimate from the specified randomized purchase endpoint.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based pilot: USD 299/month per merchant, justified only if net incremental contribution exceeds the fee and implementation cost.
candidates.costControl: Cache capability checks by app/configuration version and revalidate on changes; avoid creating payment sessions merely to inspect a browsing cart.
dependencies: Control of the agent or supported channel integration
Supported checkout escalation and buyer confirmation
candidates.failureMode: An extra handoff slows working checkouts; manifests become stale; channels already solve the issue for most carts.
candidates.falsifier: Affected missions show no positive purchase effect, or gains disappear after counting purchases through alternative channels.

candidates.title: Offer a verified arrival plan for deadline-driven shopping
candidates.buyer: Merchants selling gifts, event supplies or urgent replacement parts to AI shoppers who provide a delivery deadline.
candidates.problem: Generic shipping FAQs cannot determine whether a particular variant can reach a particular buyer before the event. Overconfident promises can cause cancellations and returns.
candidates.mechanism: Stage: selection and fulfillment. Restricting recommendations to executable fulfillment plans can convert otherwise uncertain shopping missions into paid purchases that arrive in time.
candidates.intervention: Combine merchant inventory, warehouse cutoff, carrier service and buyer-provided destination into an expiring plan. Distinguish ship date from estimated arrival. Refresh the plan at purchase and offer honest alternatives if it fails; show a guarantee only where the merchant actually underwrites it.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already has live stock, cart context, shipping calculations and Knowledge Base policies. The hypothesized edge is validating a specific buyer deadline against fulfillment evidence, rather than adding an estimated-delivery sentence.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Deadline feasibility explains a material abandonment segment and improves on-time retained purchases more than generic shipping copy.

Primary endpoint: paid orders delivered by the requested date and retained after the return window per assigned mission. Enroll across 6-8 weeks including ordinary periods; power on actual deadline demand. Both arms must use truthful promises. Guard margins, expedited shipping cost and late deliveries.
candidates.metric: On-time retained paid purchases / randomized deadline-bearing missions. Total paid-order rate and deadline failure rate are secondary; do not add them as separate uplift.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. cart-checkout and kb-faq document inputs and native overlap. ftc-shipping supports the need for a reasonable basis for shipment promises, not a conversion estimate or an arrival guarantee.

impactScenario.baseline: No empirical baseline. Let N be deadline missions, pT and pC their on-time retained purchase rates, m contribution and c extra fulfillment cost.
impactScenario.calculation: Net value = N*(pT-pC)*m - c - service cost. An increase in checkout completions alone is insufficient.
impactScenario.range: No evidence-based lift range. Zero or negative effects remain possible; estimate from the specified randomized purchase endpoint.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based pilot: USD 399/month plus separately agreed integration work; merchant tests willingness using retained contribution rather than gross revenue.
candidates.costControl: Use cached service calendars for initial filtering and obtain a live quote only for shortlisted, purchase-ready items.
dependencies: Merchant authority to make or amend promises
candidates.failureMode: Overly conservative filtering hides products that would arrive; expensive shipping erases margin; promised arrival exceeds available evidence.
candidates.falsifier: The verified plan does not improve on-time retained purchase rate or costs more contribution than it creates.

candidates.title: Prove a replacement part fits before recommending a substitute
candidates.buyer: Parts, accessories and technical-product merchants whose AI shoppers have an exact compatibility requirement.
candidates.problem: Similarity, normalized catalog attributes or frequently bought-together data can suggest a plausible item that does not fit the customer's existing equipment.
candidates.mechanism: Stage: product selection. Verified compatibility and constrained substitution can turn an unavailable exact item into an acceptable paid replacement while avoiding mismatch returns.
candidates.intervention: Build a merchant/manufacturer-supported graph of compatibility conditions, exclusions and valid substitutions. Require an exact model or buyer-confirmed measurements, cite the supporting record, and abstain when evidence is incomplete. Use catalog search to retrieve candidates, then a deterministic verifier to qualify them.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already groups variants and offers related/complementary recommendations. Global Catalog marks some technical fields as inferred. The added capability is evidence-backed constraint checking, not another recommendation carousel; specialist fitment vendors may already serve each vertical.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A narrow vertical with well-maintained compatibility records has enough avoidable mismatch and unavailable-item abandonment to support a verified substitution layer.
dataNeeded: Licensed manufacturer fitment tables and version identifiers
SKU/variant identity crosswalks and stock state
Paid orders and reason-coded incompatibility returns
candidates.experiment: Randomize compatibility-bearing AI missions to verified substitutes or current merchant recommendation flow, with both arms displaying existing warnings. Primary endpoint: paid order without compatibility return per mission after the category's return window. Plan 6-12 weeks plus outcome maturation; cluster repeated users. Guard installation safety, support load and unsupported compatibility claims.
candidates.metric: Retained compatible paid orders / all assigned eligible missions; report false-fit rate and margin separately.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. recommendations, mapping and global-catalog establish native overlap and inferred-data limits. No direct conversion evidence was found for this proposed system.

impactScenario.baseline: Let N be compatibility missions, a the observed share currently ending without an acceptable item, and r the net share rescued by a verified substitute.
impactScenario.calculation: Potential retained purchases = N*a*r minus any extra false-fit returns and displaced existing purchases. Values must be measured in the pilot.
impactScenario.range: No evidence-based lift range. Zero or negative effects remain possible; estimate from the specified randomized purchase endpoint.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: USD 599/month for a narrowly scoped parts catalog; test against incremental contribution plus avoided return handling, without double counting.
candidates.costControl: Pay for authoritative fitment data and deterministic validation first; use language models for request normalization and explanations, not as the source of compatibility truth.
candidates.failureMode: Catalog identities drift, evidence is incomplete, or the real barrier is price rather than fit confidence.
candidates.falsifier: No gain in compatible retained orders after returns, or the verifier cannot maintain a tolerable false-fit rate.

candidates.title: Let buyers carry an editable purchase brief across permitted agents
candidates.buyer: Shopping-agent platforms and merchants serving repeat shoppers with explicit recurring requirements.
candidates.problem: Account continuity does not necessarily preserve the buyer's current budget, fit constraints, intended recipient or previous rejected options. Repeating those details can derail a later purchase.
candidates.mechanism: Stage: repeat discovery and selection. Reusing a buyer-approved brief reduces repeated clarification and wrong recommendations, which could increase completed purchases per genuine shopping mission.
candidates.intervention: Offer a revocable, versioned brief containing only user-selected hard requirements, preferences, exclusions and expiry. Present a short confirmation before reuse. Connect to supported identity flows without exporting entire chat histories or granting payment authority by implication.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already documents buyer-linked Shop token exchange. Its Global Catalog page labels personalized search coming soon, despite broader language in the auth overview. The edge is explicit portable intent with expiry and correction, beyond login or inferred personalization.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: User-controlled intent transfer outperforms account identity alone for shoppers whose requirements recur but can change between missions.

candidates.experiment: Randomize consenting returning buyers to ordinary supported identity or identity plus reusable brief. Primary endpoint: retained paid purchases per randomized buyer over 8 weeks. Stratify by prior shopping frequency, analyze intention to treat even if no new mission begins, and power on buyers rather than prompts. Guard consent withdrawals, unwanted disclosure, wrong-recipient purchases and returns.
candidates.metric: Retained purchases per assigned buyer and contribution per buyer; per-mission conversion is secondary because the brief may change mission frequency.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. buyer-token, auth and global-catalog establish existing identity and availability constraints. They provide no measured value for a portable preference brief.

impactScenario.range: No evidence-based lift range. Zero or negative effects remain possible; estimate from the specified randomized purchase endpoint.

candidates.costControl: Store compact explicit constraints and reusable identifiers instead of entire transcripts; refresh only expired or changed facts.
dependencies: Explicit user choice rather than covert sensitive profiling
candidates.failureMode: Few buyers reuse briefs, requirements become stale, privacy friction outweighs saved effort, or platforms keep intent inside their own systems.
candidates.falsifier: Returning-buyer retained purchases do not improve or brief reuse causes more requirement mismatches and returns.

candidates.title: Recover delayed AI orders with a truthful replacement choice
candidates.buyer: US merchants whose AI-originated physical-goods orders encounter fulfillment delays.
candidates.problem: A delayed order can become a refund even when a buyer would prefer an available, suitable alternative. Required delay notices and refund choices must remain clear.
candidates.mechanism: Stage: post-purchase retention. Timely, accurate alternatives with explicit buyer choice could preserve paid purchases that would otherwise be cancelled; this is retained-order value, not new customer acquisition.
candidates.intervention: On a forecast missed ship promise, prepare the existing delay/refund options plus a verified in-stock replacement with its price difference and supported ship estimate. Obtain explicit acceptance before editing the order or collecting more payment. Preserve the original promise, notice and choice record; never obstruct a refund.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already supplies order lifecycle state and editing workflows, and ordinary support teams offer replacements. The edge is evidence-checked alternatives tied to the original AI shopping requirements and a timely choice workflow. End-to-end support for this exact workflow was not established in reviewed native docs.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Merchants can retain more satisfactory paid orders by offering an acceptable available alternative at the same moment they disclose a delay.
dataNeeded: Original item, buyer-approved requirements and ship promise
OMS delay forecasts and authoritative substitute stock
Notice timestamps, explicit choices, refunds and fulfillment outcomes
candidates.experiment: Randomize affected AI-originated orders to the merchant's timely compliant delay/refund notice or the same options plus a verified replacement. Primary endpoint: paid orders fulfilled and retained after the replacement return window per assigned affected order. Enroll 8-12 weeks or until powered. Both arms receive required disclosures and refund rights; monitor complaints, unwanted substitutions and support effort.
candidates.metric: Retained fulfilled paid orders / all randomized delay-affected orders. Report refund processing time and satisfaction alongside it; do not count an edited order as a second purchase.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. ftc-shipping establishes shipment-promise/delay/refund duties in its stated US scope, not legal approval of this design. order-webhooks and order-mcp establish technical state access, with authorization constraints.

impactScenario.baseline: Let D be delay-affected AI orders and rT-rC the difference in legitimately retained fulfilled-order probability.
impactScenario.calculation: Retained purchases = D*(rT-rC). Value subtracts substitute cost, extra shipping, refunds and service expense. Acquisition uplift is zero by definition for this retention intervention.
impactScenario.range: No evidence-based lift range. Zero or negative effects remain possible; estimate from the specified randomized purchase endpoint.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: USD 199/month per merchant, evaluated against incremental retained contribution and operating cost.
candidates.costControl: Deterministically match stock and constraints; route ambiguous substitutions to staff. Use lifecycle events instead of polling order APIs.
dependencies: Merchant-approved notice requirements and refund process
Partner-manager setup for UCP order webhooks, or authorized merchant order access
candidates.failureMode: Alternatives disappoint buyers or create pressure to accept; delays are rare; operational cost exceeds retained contribution.
candidates.falsifier: No improvement in satisfactory retained orders, slower refunds, or any systematic increase in unwanted substitutions.

candidates.title: Optimize an entire shopping mission across executable baskets
candidates.buyer: Independent shopping agents or merchant consortia serving multi-item missions such as furnishing a room or assembling a kit.
candidates.problem: Individually attractive recommendations can become an unaffordable or incomplete basket after shipping, compatibility constraints and unavailable components are considered.
candidates.mechanism: Stage: basket formation. A complete feasible plan reduces arithmetic and coordination work, allowing more buyers to purchase the mission they actually intended to complete.
candidates.intervention: Compare a small set of whole-basket plans under the buyer's budget, delivery and substitution permissions. Calculate current seller-specific shipping/discount totals, explain tradeoffs, and preserve separate seller commitments. Use merchant-scoped checkouts now; integrate Universal Cart only after approved access.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already has cart tools, complementary recommendations and an early-access Universal Cart offering. The additional hypothesis is a constraint-aware whole-mission optimizer, not merely a shared cart or extra add-ons.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Whole-basket feasibility can recover missions that product-by-product ranking loses, without increasing buyer spend through unnecessary items.

Cross-seller SKU identity, permitted substitutes and compatibility
Paid line items, returns and mission completion

Primary endpoint: an agreed complete basket purchased and retained per assigned mission. Run 6-8 weeks plus return maturation; power on missions. Track spending against stated budget, margin by seller, return rates and abandoned partial purchases.
candidates.metric: Completed retained paid baskets / randomized eligible missions. Do not claim uplift from splitting one basket into more orders; report component purchases only as secondary.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. agents, cart-checkout and recommendations document adjacent infrastructure, not a causal basket-planning benefit.

impactScenario.baseline: Let N be eligible missions and bT-bC the causal difference in complete retained basket purchase probability.
impactScenario.calculation: Added completed purchases = N*(bT-bC). Evaluate merchant contribution across all participating sellers and subtract integration/service cost.
impactScenario.range: No evidence-based lift range. Zero or negative effects remain possible; estimate from the specified randomized purchase endpoint.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot: USD 1,000/month per agent platform or consortium. Validate payment against measured mission completion and transparent commercial terms.
candidates.costControl: Prune infeasible combinations using deterministic bounds and cached catalogs; live-quote only the few complete plans the buyer could reasonably choose.
dependencies: Current totals and permissible cart creation
A workable sequence of individual checkouts or Universal Cart early access
candidates.failureMode: The plan optimizes a measurable budget while missing taste; multi-checkout friction remains; benefits accrue to consumers or rivals without a paying buyer.
candidates.falsifier: Complete retained purchase probability fails to rise, or apparent gains come only from more split orders or unwanted items.

candidates.title: Honor the buyer's valid quoted item price without a support detour
candidates.buyer: Merchants with frequent promotions or price experiments whose AI-referral shoppers see different price versions.
candidates.problem: A shopper can encounter one product price in an AI result and another at the merchant. Manual price-honor policies add friction even when the merchant is willing to honor a valid earlier quote.
candidates.mechanism: Stage: checkout completion. Automatically recognizing a legitimate quote can preserve trust and remove a support interruption, increasing paid purchases at the same agreed economics.

Existing merchant price-honor policy and margin limits

Primary endpoint: retained paid purchases per mission within 7 days. Run 4-8 weeks and power on real quote disagreements; guard abuse, margin and currency errors. Do not manufacture inaccurate quotes for the test.
