candidates.title: Test honest inventory holds without mistaking displacement for growth
candidates.buyer: Merchants with scarce variants and considered AI shopping missions that take time to complete.
candidates.problem: A product can sell out during a lengthy decision, but reserving stock can deprive other buyers of the same unit. More conversions among held carts need not mean more merchant purchases.
candidates.mechanism: Stage: decision-to-checkout. A buyer-requested, short inventory hold might keep a feasible purchase alive; merchant-wide experiments must show that recovered sales exceed displaced sales.
candidates.intervention: Use native reservations for explicit buyer-requested holds, with transparent expiry and no urgency copy. Add a bounded allocation policy based on stock depth, expected replenishment and a buyer-selected decision window. Release unused holds promptly and do not fabricate scarcity.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify draft orders already reserve inventory and expose expiry. The new hypothesis is a demand-aware allocation policy evaluated against total retained orders across affected stock, not a hold button or countdown.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Some inventory pools can support bounded decision time while increasing total fulfilled purchases, rather than merely reallocating the last unit to another buyer.
dataNeeded: SKU-level available/committed inventory and restock times
Hold expiry, redemption and other-channel lost-sales signals
All-channel retained purchases for affected inventory pools
candidates.experiment: Randomize comparable SKU-inventory-pool by week clusters to the bounded hold policy or existing no-hold/manual-hold process; avoid individual randomization because units are shared. Primary endpoint: all-channel retained paid orders from each assigned pool, with AI-origin orders separately reported. Run across several replenishment cycles, typically 8-12 weeks, and power on pools. Guard stock starvation, bot abuse and customer fairness.
candidates.metric: Retained paid orders per randomized inventory-pool period, adjusted by prespecified stock exposure. AI hold redemption is diagnostic only; it cannot establish incrementality.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. draft-orders confirms the reservation primitive. No evidence currently establishes that an agent-specific allocation policy increases total purchases.

impactScenario.baseline: Let R be recovered AI purchases, L displaced purchases from all other buyers and U additional losses from unusable held stock, all measured over the same replenishment window.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental retained purchases = R - L - U. A high hold redemption rate can coexist with zero or negative incrementality.
impactScenario.range: No evidence-based lift range. Zero or negative effects remain possible; estimate from the specified randomized purchase endpoint.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot price: USD 299/month per merchant. Charge only where all-channel contribution supports the cost; scarce-stock stores may have no incremental-demand opportunity.

candidates.title: Keep the recommended width and inseam available until checkout
candidates.buyer: Footwear and denim merchants with fragmented variant inventory
candidates.problem: A shopper accepts a fit recommendation but the exact width, inseam or regional size is unavailable or mismapped when the cart opens.
candidates.mechanism: Selection to checkout: prevent a stale or wrong-variant promise from destroying purchase intent, while preserving a shopper-approved alternative when fulfilment is genuinely possible.
candidates.intervention: Attach size-system and fit-version identifiers to the result, revalidate the exact variant against authoritative stock at handoff, and offer a short merchant-supported reservation after explicit add-to-cart intent. Reconfirm material substitutions; do not silently choose a different fit.
candidates.competitorOverlap: True Fit already filters by recommended-size availability, and Fit Analytics Product Suggestions finds alternatives. The proposed edge is a verified, time-bounded path from recommendation to the same purchasable variant.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Reservation and fresh variant validation add value beyond merely hiding out-of-stock products.
dataNeeded: Fulfilment failures and matured purchase outcomes
candidates.experiment: Randomize shoppers at fit acceptance to current availability filtering or validation plus optional reservation. Primary is retained purchase within 7 days, matured through return expiry. Run 6-8 weeks plus maturation and power for observed stock-failure prevalence. If holds affect other shoppers materially, randomize independent stock pools instead; guard stock hoarding, checkout latency, cancellations and spillovers.
candidates.metric: Difference in retained-purchaser rate among all assigned fit-accepting shoppers; preserve nonbuyers in the denominator and deduplicate replacement orders.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. tf-agent and fa-simons establish existing availability-aware recommendations, not causal evidence for reservation.

impactScenario.baseline: Let N be observed eligible handoffs and f their measured stock/mapping failure fraction; both unknown before instrumentation.
impactScenario.calculation: Maximum addressable pool is N*f. Additional retained purchasers = N*f*(recovery improvement) minus lost purchasers caused by delay or displaced stock; all terms must be estimated.
impactScenario.range: Can be zero when existing filtering is fresh, or negative when reservations displace more sales than they rescue.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot price: GBP 750/month; compare with contribution from incremental retained purchases and reservation costs.
candidates.costControl: Recheck stock on decision transitions, not every generated token; cache stable size mappings separately from volatile inventory.
candidates.failureMode: Holds create artificial stockouts or size mappings confuse a wide fit with a longer shoe.
candidates.falsifier: Failures are too rare to meet break-even, or the experiment only shifts purchases between shoppers without net gain.

candidates.title: Count substitute families before declaring a catalog winner
candidates.buyer: Multi-brand retailer or marketplace experimentation team with many interchangeable SKUs
candidates.problem: A winning product page may take purchases from sibling products or control pages. SKU-level gains can therefore overstate additional merchant purchases.
candidates.mechanism: Enabling layer for discovery and selection: group products that compete for the same shopping mission, measure merchant-level incremental orders, and deploy interventions that recruit or complete purchases rather than merely redistribute them.
candidates.intervention: Build a substitution graph from consented aggregate co-view, comparison, switch and return/exchange histories plus product identity. Keep dense substitute families within an assignment unit, randomize matched families, and report recipient, donor and combined order effects with spillover diagnostics.
candidates.competitorOverlap: SearchPilot already studies linked source and destination groups and discusses cross-page redistribution. This proposal extends assignment to observed shopper substitution, sibling variants and order outcomes. Cluster experimentation also exists in marketplace research; it is not a new statistical invention.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Substitution-aware assignment rejects more false merchant-growth wins without sacrificing enough statistical power to erase its commercial benefit.
dataNeeded: Aggregate product switching and co-consideration graph
Orders covering all products in each family
candidates.experiment: Randomize matched substitute-family clusters to the same proposed discovery intervention or unchanged treatment. Primary endpoint: total retained merchant orders generated by the assigned families over at least eight weeks plus the return window. Define order-to-family allocation before launch and count a mixed basket once. Run a meta-experiment across portfolios comparing this design's rollout decisions with ordinary page splits. Use cluster-robust uncertainty, pre-period adjustment and boundary diagnostics; the effective sample is families, not URLs. Guardrails: all-channel order totals, stock depletion and spillovers.
candidates.metric: Difference in retained orders per randomized family over a fixed horizon, accompanied by observed AI-labelled orders and all-channel totals. Do not divide by treatment-generated sessions or sum overlapping SKU effects.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase benefit. interference provides adjacent causal evidence that marketplace listing experiments can suffer interference. sp-linking proves SearchPilot already addresses some cross-page effects.

impactScenario.baseline: Chosen illustration: 100,000 monthly category visits and 2,000 merchant orders across a substitute family.
impactScenario.calculation: A treated SKU gains 100 orders while siblings lose 100, so merchant incrementality is 100 - 100 = 0 despite the SKU winner. If the sibling loss were 120, merchant impact would be -20; if it were 40, impact would be +60.
impactScenario.range: These are accounting sensitivities, not predicted effects. The measurement product can have zero benefit when substitution is negligible and negative value if clustering makes useful tests too slow.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: USD 2,000 per large catalog experiment. Break even only if the contribution from avoided false rollouts and better winners exceeds this fee and the loss of testing speed.
candidates.costControl: Use sparse aggregate graphs and refresh clusters only after material assortment changes. Restrict graph complexity to boundaries that can alter a purchase decision.
dependencies: Merchant permission for aggregate behavioral data
candidates.failureMode: Substitution can cross the chosen boundaries; poor clustering can increase variance; broad category clusters may leave too few randomization units; external competitors remain unobserved.
candidates.falsifier: Boundary-adjusted retained-order conclusions and prospective rollout value do not improve over ordinary page splits, or power loss prevents decisions within the selling horizon.

candidates.buyer: Retailer with regional stock, collection options and deadline-sensitive AI referral traffic
candidates.problem: The product selected during an AI conversation may no longer arrive by the shopper's required date when checkout starts, causing a lost order even when a suitable alternative is available.
candidates.mechanism: Selection-to-purchase recovery: ask for the shopper's actual deadline, compare it with current fulfillment promises, and present an acceptable alternative before the shopper abandons or places an order that will be cancelled.
candidates.intervention: At a merchant-owned landing or approved agent handoff, offer an optional need-by date and delivery region check. Compare the current accurate availability experience with the verified alternatives. Primary endpoint: orders delivered by the stated date and retained through the return window per assigned eligible shopper. Guardrails: promise misses, cost-to-serve, gross margin, substitution complaints and page latency. No invented urgency.

impactScenario.calculation: If the intervention creates a hypothetical 5 percentage-point increase in on-time completed purchases within the 800 failures, extra retained orders = 10,000 * 0.08 * 0.05 * 0.90 = 36, before additional fulfillment cost.

candidates.intervention: Bind product, variant, seller and offer IDs to verified condition, warranty-provider and policy-version records. At a seller or offer change, show which terms changed and request confirmation. Resolve missing terms as unknown; never infer authorized-dealer status from branding or a GTIN.
candidates.competitorOverlap: OpenAI's checkout contract already uses selected merchant offer IDs and authoritative merchant data. Its feed schema already separates brand and seller. Google and native commerce systems already represent offer-level policies. The edge is tested continuity of seller-specific promises, not entity mapping itself; incumbent support may be broader than public sources.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: In journeys with multiple valid sellers or conditions, explicit promise continuity produces more retained purchases and fewer disputes than the existing product-to-offer handoff.
candidates.experiment: Randomize shopper-level eligible multi-offer journeys to the existing compliant handoff or the continuity check. Hold product availability and mandatory disclosures constant. Primary endpoint: retained completed orders per assigned journey over eight weeks plus return maturity; guardrails include seller-confusion complaints, disputes, price, confirmation abandonment and unauthorized-claim incidence. Stratify by observed offer switches without selecting the primary sample after treatment. OpenAI beta access is a dependency for inline checkout; merchant-owned referral pages can be tested sooner.
candidates.metric: Retained merchant orders per assigned eligible shopper; report product-level demand, seller switching and destination retailer separately. A sale merely transferred among the buyer's own sellers is not automatically incremental marketplace demand.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. openai-checkout and openai-products establish native identity requirements. No direct evidence was found for retained-order uplift from the proposed promise continuity layer.

impactScenario.baseline: Chosen example: 20,000 identifiable AI-origin offer journeys/month, 5% with genuinely ambiguous or changed seller terms, 90% retention.
impactScenario.calculation: If the 1,000 affected journeys gain a hypothetical 3 percentage-point completion improvement, incremental retained orders = 20,000 * 0.05 * 0.03 * 0.90 = 27. Dispute reduction is counted separately from added orders.
impactScenario.range: Zero if current handoffs already preserve terms; negative if extra choice prompts reduce completion or the verification data is wrong.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot: USD 800/month for a multi-seller catalog. At USD 40 contribution per additional retained order, 20 incremental orders/month cover the fee before verification operations.
candidates.costControl: Verify at seller-policy-version level and reuse results across relevant offers. Refresh on changes instead of asking an LLM to regenerate promises per session.
candidates.failureMode: The merchant may lack reliable warranty authority; offer identity can change unexpectedly; policy complexity may overwhelm shoppers; the service may simply expose unattractive terms and reduce purchases.
candidates.falsifier: A powered test produces no retained-order gain or higher disputes, or most observed ambiguities cannot be resolved from reliable evidence.

candidates.title: Make the simulator earn its right to choose live tests
candidates.buyer: Merchant experimentation platform or agency considering a synthetic-shopping product
candidates.problem: A simulator can prefer text or rankings that influence its own agents but do not change production AI discovery or human purchases. Repeated runs can give precise answers to the wrong question.
candidates.mechanism: Enabling selection layer: calibrate simulated failure diagnoses against held-out live purchase experiments, use only the parts that improve intervention selection, and allocate scarce live tests to changes that produce more real retained orders.
candidates.intervention: Create a versioned benchmark of frozen tool responses, distinct consented shopping intents and merchant interventions paired with blinded live purchase results. Measure selection accuracy and calibration across held-out merchants and model versions. Treat rank swaps as oracle sensitivities, not deployable actions. Gate use of simulator recommendations on prospective portfolio performance.
candidates.competitorOverlap: SearchPilot already published a multi-turn shopper toy experiment. Shopify SimGym provides synthetic shopper/theme comparisons, and Rollouts offers live experiments. Lily Max already links hypotheses to tests. The proposed advantage is validated simulation-to-purchase transfer, not simulation plus A/B testing.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A simulator that passes merchant-held-out validation can select a portfolio with more incremental retained AI-origin orders than experts or random selection at the same total testing budget.
dataNeeded: Frozen retrieval/tool payloads and version hashes
Distinct real shopping missions with consent and no sensitive profiling
Blinded randomized purchase outcomes and return states
Model, tool, engine and cost versions
candidates.experiment: First freeze training and evaluation merchants before viewing outcomes. Then randomize independent merchant/category portfolios to expert-selected, randomly selected or simulator-selected feasible interventions, each with equal live testing and engineering budgets. Randomize the underlying merchant interventions at shopper or catalog-family level as appropriate. Primary endpoint: total incremental retained AI-labelled orders across the portfolio over a prespecified quarter plus returns, not synthetic recommendation share. Power on portfolios and real purchases; 50 reruns of one persona are not 50 consumer observations. Guardrails: all-channel orders, harmful recommendations and implementation cost.
candidates.metric: Prospective portfolio difference in incremental retained AI-labelled orders at equal cost. Held-out ranking accuracy is a prerequisite diagnostic. Report observable AI provenance only, and never label offline simulated recommendation rates as current ChatGPT rates.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. sp-conversations is direct evidence of research overlap but no purchase validation. shopify-simgym is product overlap and explicitly warns of behavioral differences; shopify-rollouts supplies live testing primitives.

impactScenario.baseline: Chosen example: ten equal-cost candidate live-test slots per quarter. Existing selection finds two useful interventions, each producing 30 incremental retained orders over the fixed horizon.
impactScenario.calculation: If simulator selection finds three equally valuable interventions, the difference is (3 - 2) * 30 = 30 retained orders. At USD 25 contribution each this is USD 750 before simulator and integration cost. These assumed hit rates and effects require independent validation.
impactScenario.range: Zero if both selectors find equivalent interventions; negative if simulated winners do not transfer, if it misses useful changes, or if generation cost exceeds the extra purchase value.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot price: USD 500 per merchant-quarter for experiment selection, conditional on benchmark and prospective lift. SimGym's USD 1.50 post-allowance comparison price makes raw simulation runs a weak pricing anchor.
candidates.costControl: Reuse fixed payloads and paired random seeds for variance reduction, while sampling genuinely different intents. Stop resampling a persona once uncertainty is smaller than the next live-test decision requires.
dependencies: A sufficiently large independent live-experiment library
candidates.failureMode: Benchmark leakage, synthetic persona bias, model updates and merchant mismatch can create false transfer. A simulator can learn to predict traffic metrics while failing on retained orders.
candidates.falsifier: Prospective equal-budget portfolios fail to outperform expert or random selection on retained purchases, even if simulated recommendation and add-to-cart rates improve.

candidates.title: Prove that the whole project basket works
candidates.buyer: DIY, electronics and specialist outdoor retailers with multi-item AI shopping missions
candidates.problem: A plausible list of individually relevant products can omit a required part or contain an incompatible combination, so the shopper cannot confidently buy the project.
candidates.mechanism: Selection to purchase: translate the stated job into explicit requirements, resolve all required dependencies and show one feasible basket. Fewer missing-part doubts should create additional completed project orders; larger basket value alone is not success.
candidates.intervention: Build a constraint solver over exact variants, required-part relationships, quantities and total budget. Return a feasible basket with evidence for each dependency, plus a clear unresolved item when data is missing. Keep optional accessories visibly optional.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Constructor ASA already handles multi-item goals; Google supports required_part relationships; Channable advertises forthcoming bundles. A constraint-checked complete basket is an edge hypothesis, not claimed category novelty.

Primary endpoint: at least one paid mission order within 14 days, retained at 45 days. Plan 6 to 8 weeks plus return maturation, powered from observed baseline/MDE. Guardrails: total purchase rate, missing-part returns, price, latency and no unapproved substitutions.
candidates.metric: Retained mission purchasers / all randomized eligible mission shoppers; report absolute ITT difference. Completed-basket share and AOV are secondary and cannot substitute for more purchasers.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; adjacent agent-use association in belk and existing capabilities in asa/google-attrs/channable do not supply an expected lift.

impactScenario.baseline: Chosen example only: 10,000 eligible shoppers/month, GBP 80 contribution per retained incremental order, GBP 2,000 monthly fee; baseline conversion and fault prevalence unknown.
impactScenario.calculation: Fee-only break-even = 2000 / 80 = 25 extra retained orders, or 25 / 10000 = 0.25 percentage points. Add integration and serving costs before deciding.
impactScenario.range: No predicted effect; zero if existing recommendations already solve the job, negative if strict checks exclude valid combinations.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP 2,000/month, with integration quoted separately; validate willingness to pay against incremental retained contribution.
candidates.costControl: Cache verified dependency graphs and solve deterministic constraints before calling an LLM. Preserve checks for genuinely ambiguous assemblies.
candidates.failureMode: Incorrect graph edges create false confidence, or incomplete data makes a useful basket impossible to recommend.
candidates.falsifier: A powered test finds no retained-purchase improvement or a rise in compatibility failures versus the same-data comparator.

candidates.title: Ask only the question that changes the purchase decision
candidates.buyer: Merchants whose AI shopping agent repeatedly asks shoppers to refine broad requests
candidates.problem: An extra clarification can prevent an unsuitable recommendation, but unnecessary dialogue can also lose a shopper who is ready to buy.
candidates.mechanism: Selection to purchase: estimate whether an unresolved fact changes the set of suitable products; ask one short question only when that information is more valuable than the resulting delay. Otherwise expose a usable shortlist immediately.
candidates.intervention: Build a question-selection and stopping policy using candidate-set disagreement, mandatory requirements and observed abandonment. Allow a skip path and show why a fact matters; do not infer sensitive traits or fabricate certainty.
candidates.competitorOverlap: ASA and PIA already ask follow-ups and retain context. The proposed difference is a purchase-validated decision about when to stop asking, rather than a new chat capability.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A calibrated stop/ask policy produces more paid purchases per eligible conversation than a fixed follow-up strategy at equal recommendation quality.
dataNeeded: Order linkage and product suitability returns
candidates.experiment: Randomize shoppers at their first eligible ambiguous AI query to existing follow-ups or the policy. Primary: paid purchase within 7 days; retain assignment across turns. Plan 4 to 6 weeks, calculate power from query prevalence and baseline, then mature returns. Guardrails: inappropriate recommendations, skip rate, customer-reported confusion and total purchases.
candidates.metric: Paid purchasers within 7 days / all randomized eligible shoppers, including those who decline or abandon the question; report returns separately and reject a gain caused by unsuitable purchases.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; agent-api and pia establish overlap, while demo's use-conditioned claims cannot quantify this intervention.

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative assumptions: 10,000 eligible ambiguous-query shoppers/month, GBP 30 incremental-order contribution, GBP 750 monthly fee; no measured baseline or clarification-failure prevalence.
impactScenario.calculation: 750 / 30 = 25 extra retained purchases; 25 / 10000 = 0.25 percentage points fee-only break-even.
impactScenario.range: Zero if existing follow-ups are already well calibrated; negative if skipping questions conceals a decisive constraint.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 750/month plus serving costs; require enough measured incremental contribution to cover both.
candidates.costControl: Use deterministic candidate divergence and a small classifier for the stop decision. Reserve larger-model questions for ambiguous cases.
candidates.failureMode: The policy optimizes fast purchases while omitting a fact that would have prevented a return.
candidates.falsifier: Paid purchase gains disappear after returns, or the policy cannot beat a simple one-question rule.

candidates.title: Resolve the shopper's actual offer eligibility before quoting savings
candidates.buyer: Loyalty-heavy or headless Shopify merchants with segment-specific promotions
candidates.problem: Price/checkout: a shopper arriving from AI shopping sees an advertised offer but cannot establish whether it applies to their account and cart.
candidates.mechanism: An authenticated, authoritative eligibility result prevents surprise pricing and resolves a concrete checkout objection. Any lift must exceed discount cannibalization and login friction.
candidates.intervention: Read the merchant's promotion evaluator with shopper permission, return the exact eligible cart total and exclusions, and offer guest checkout when no identity-based benefit exists. Compare an applied eligible offer against the same offer discovered later at checkout; do not create a new discount by default.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Gorgias already creates coupons and detects automatic promotions, but its docs exclude segment-targeted automatic discounts and headless detection. Alhena has authenticated custom tools, so API-based eligibility is an implementation edge, not a new category.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Showing a verified applicable existing offer closes more AI-origin purchases than generic discount language that is incomplete for these segments.
dataNeeded: External-AI referral/origin recorded before treatment; self-declared origin kept separate
Promotion rules and authoritative cart evaluator
Actual applied discount and net order margin
candidates.experiment: Primary cohort: verified external-AI-origin arrivals; report self-declared and unknown origin separately. Randomize eligible AI-origin shoppers before the offer-verification invitation; compare standard promotion messaging with optional verified eligibility. Primary: 7-day paid purchase per assigned shopper, with retained margin and total discount cost as guardrails. Enroll through 4-8 weeks including a complete promotion cycle and power analysis; stratify existing members and guests.
candidates.metric: Purchase-rate difference per assigned shopper, not per authenticated member. Count failed authentication and rejected offers. Track contribution after actual discounts.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized, supported by a documented coverage boundary in g-discount and adjacent authenticated tooling in alhena-context. No measured gain transferred.

impactScenario.baseline: Hypothetical merchant: 10000 eligible, verified external-AI-origin shoppers per month; 3% buy and retain at least one item; USD 40 contribution per additional retained purchase after merchandise, fulfillment and expected returns. These are chosen assumptions, not observations.
impactScenario.calculation: Monthly incremental contribution = 10000 * (p_treatment - p_control) * USD 40 - additional operating costs - USD 400 fee. Ignoring additional operating costs, covering the fee requires 10 additional retained purchases (0.100 percentage points). Include all human, API, discount and integration costs before a buying decision.
impactScenario.range: No supported uplift range. Zero or negative purchase effects are possible; break-even is a decision threshold, not a forecast.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test: USD 400/month where promotion confusion is observed; merchant must value resolved orders above integration and discount costs.
candidates.costControl: Use the existing promotion engine and short-lived cached eligibility, invalidated on cart/account changes; avoid discretionary coupons.
candidates.failureMode: Authentication friction exceeds benefit, exclusions disappoint shoppers, or stale eligibility produces a checkout mismatch.
candidates.falsifier: Verified offers do not improve purchases or produce lower retained contribution than the existing promotion experience.

candidates.title: Recover unavailable AI recommendations without losing the original constraints
candidates.buyer: Multi-region merchants with stock-sensitive variants and chat/email/SMS shopping
candidates.problem: Availability/selection: an AI-origin shopper asks about an unavailable product in email or SMS, or before the assistant knows region; a merely similar alternative can violate the reason they chose it.
candidates.mechanism: Check exact sellable variant and region, preserve the user's non-negotiable constraints, and offer only feasible substitutes. Recoverable unavailable-item demand becomes a real purchasable alternative.
candidates.intervention: Add a region-confirmed availability check to every substitute decision across channels. Maintain a small constraint ledger, verify alternatives against it, and produce one live checkout link. If no alternative qualifies, explain the failed constraint and offer an optional restock alert with no false urgency.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Gorgias already filters region-unavailable products in chat with documented exceptions; similar recommendations and Shopify carts exist. The experiment targets cross-channel exceptions and constraint preservation, not generic stock filtering.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Constraint-preserving substitutes recover more retained orders than normal similarity suggestions for the documented exception paths.
dataNeeded: External-AI referral/origin recorded before treatment; self-declared origin kept separate
Authoritative sellable inventory at variant level
Orders, stock failures and return reasons
candidates.experiment: Primary cohort: verified external-AI-origin arrivals; report self-declared and unknown origin separately. Randomize shopper-level eligible unavailable-item conversations to ordinary truthful availability assistance or the checked substitute flow. Primary: 14-day paid purchase from any qualifying substitute. Run at least 8 weeks if required for enough stockout cases; precompute power from observed fault prevalence. Guardrails wrong variants, backorders, return rate and latency.
candidates.metric: Any qualifying purchase per all assigned stockout shoppers; do not count multiple alternative clicks as wins. Report sitewide contribution as this effect times independently measured eligible prevalence, without overlapping other recovery cohorts.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; g-recommend documents the triggering limitations. shopify-cart supplies existing checkout infrastructure, not an uplift claim.

Ignoring additional operating costs, covering the fee requires 12 additional retained purchases (0.240 percentage points). Include all human, API, discount and integration costs before a buying decision.
impactScenario.range: No supported uplift range. Zero or negative purchase effects are possible; break-even is a decision threshold, not a forecast.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test: USD 450/month for a merchant with enough actual exception-path demand; test against existing Gorgias setup before selling.
candidates.costControl: Fetch inventory only for the original variant and a bounded substitute set; short cache with inventory-event invalidation.

candidates.title: Turn the shopper's real deadline into a feasible delivery choice
candidates.buyer: Gift, events, furniture, parts and outdoor merchants with time-sensitive AI referrals
candidates.problem: Fulfillment/checkout: an externally recommended product fits the need but may not reach the shopper before an event or repair deadline.
candidates.mechanism: Translate the actual need-by date into authoritative shipping and stock options. A feasible variant, pickup location or service resolves a buying blocker; disclosing uncertainty avoids a false sale.
candidates.intervention: After an optional destination and deadline, evaluate carrier cutoff, warehouse stock and fulfillment promise for the chosen basket. Offer a factual comparison of feasible choices with cost and confidence, and revalidate immediately before checkout. Never invent a guarantee or countdown.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Narvar already offers delivery predictions, Shopify checkout handles fulfillment, and Gorgias answers shipping questions. The proposed edge is constraint-based rescue of an AI-referred shopping mission using those systems.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A verified feasible alternative converts more deadline-constrained shoppers than a generic delivery FAQ or an unqualified estimated date.

candidates.title: Build the minimum complete basket for the shopper's task
candidates.buyer: Parts, electronics, hobby and equipment merchants with dependent products
candidates.problem: Selection/cart: an AI-generated recommendation names the main item but omits a required adapter, consumable or size match; uncertainty about completeness stalls the order.
candidates.mechanism: Prove which required components are already owned, included or missing, then create the smallest compatible basket within the declared budget. The aim is more complete successful purchases, not merely a larger basket.
candidates.intervention: Create merchant-reviewed compatibility and dependency rules. Let the shopper confirm what they already own, distinguish required from optional items, check basket-wide constraints, and show one editable compatible cart with evidence for every required addition.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Constructor already recommends products across categories, Gorgias suggests complements, and Rebuy sells cart upsells. The edge is verifiable dependency completeness and minimal cost against the existing recommendation experience; generic bundling is crowded.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A minimal complete basket reduces uncertainty and incompatible orders better than affinity-based cross-sells.
dataNeeded: External-AI referral/origin recorded before treatment; self-declared origin kept separate
candidates.experiment: Primary cohort: verified external-AI-origin arrivals; report self-declared and unknown origin separately. Assign AI-origin shoppers with a declared multi-item task to ordinary complementary recommendations or the completeness checker. Primary: 14-day paid order satisfying all necessary dependencies, adjudicated from frozen rules; guardrail overall purchases, total cost and retained orders. Run 8 weeks or powered sample; never suppress known required safety information in control.
candidates.metric: Complete, compatible paid orders per assigned task shopper, followed through returns. Revenue and AOV are secondary; optional accessory attachment is not a purchase outcome.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. constructor, g-recommend and rebuy-cart establish adjacent working products, not causal support for the completeness policy.

candidates.title: Stop selling when the AI-referred shopper is ready to pay
candidates.buyer: Merchants running proactive shopping chat, cart upsells and fast checkout
candidates.problem: Checkout: a shopper who has already decided in an external AI conversation may encounter a new search prompt, coupon pitch or cross-sell that reopens the decision.
candidates.mechanism: Answer the last question, confirm the chosen variant and total, then minimize interruption. More decided shoppers may complete a purchase even if fewer conversations or add-ons occur.
candidates.intervention: Use an explicit readiness cue such as 'buy this' or a shopper-selected 'ready to checkout' control. Suppress optional prompts for that session, show a concise order check and existing checkout continuation, and keep help available without opening it automatically.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Gorgias already adapts selling style to intent; Rebuy already tests cart variants, and Shopify provides checkout continuation. The narrow hypothesis is that a measurable subset benefits from prompt suppression, not a new checkout mechanism.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A quiet completion path increases order count among decided AI referrals compared with the merchant's normal promotional flow.

candidates.experiment: Primary cohort: verified external-AI-origin arrivals; report self-declared and unknown origin separately. At the first explicit readiness event, randomize shopper-level normal flow versus optional-prompt suppression with unchanged prices. Primary: 7-day paid purchase; mature retained-purchase and contribution guardrails. Run 4-6 weeks and compute sample from actual ready-to-buy volume. Track essential disclosures, support access and checkout errors.
candidates.metric: Paid purchases per assigned ready shopper, including abandonment. Chat engagement and AOV can fall while purchase count improves; retained contribution must remain economically acceptable.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; g-search and g-faq document proactive entry points, while rebuy-ab documents an existing testing comparator. No purchase percentage asserted.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test: USD 250/month for a small orchestration layer, only after a holdout demonstrates extra retained orders.
candidates.costControl: Use a simple session flag, avoid unnecessary model calls, and reduce paid conversations only when purchase results remain better.

candidates.failureMode: Suppression hides helpful guidance or profitable offers, or readiness detection is premature.

candidates.title: Route the unresolved decision to an expert before the shopper leaves

candidates.problem: Decision/support: a referred shopper's final compatibility or suitability question needs expertise, but ordinary handover loses context or reaches an unstaffed queue.

candidates.title: Recommend against the return reason, not toward the largest basket
candidates.buyer: Apparel, beauty, furniture and equipment merchants with costly mismatch returns
candidates.problem: Selection: an AI-origin shopper may accept a confident upsell that meets broad intent but fails a specific practical requirement and is later returned.

candidates.title: Compile shopping requests into verified hard constraints
candidates.buyer: Camera-accessory, computer-peripheral and specialist equipment retailers with frequent compatibility questions.
candidates.problem: Semantic retrieval can return plausible items that violate one decisive requirement, while ordinary filters miss requirements expressed in a sentence.
candidates.mechanism: Selection stage: translate an explicit request into testable requirements, eliminate verified mismatches and expose unresolved facts. More shoppers can reach a defensible suitable choice and complete a retained purchase. External discovery improves only if an approved channel actually uses the resulting data or tool.
candidates.intervention: Build a constraint compiler with typed units, model/version relations and three states per predicate: supported, contradicted or unknown. Return an evidence-backed candidate set, its smallest conflicting constraint set when empty, and explicit alternatives the shopper can approve. Start with one category and a merchant-controlled AI landing page or retrieval endpoint.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Constructor ASA already handles natural-language filtering and refinement; constraint-based knowledge-graph recommenders exist. Constructor also advertises Answer Engine Assistants beta. A natural-language filter or generic compatibility badge is not the edge.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: For requests with several hard requirements, verified relational constraints and an explicit unknown state outperform a well-configured incumbent semantic search plus facets on retained purchases without excessive false exclusions.
dataNeeded: Consented shopper request or explicit handoff context
SKU and variant identities, canonical units and manufacturer compatibility relations
Source provenance and recency for each decisive predicate
candidates.experiment: Persistently randomize eligible shoppers before results between the compiler and the merchant's strongest configured search/facet experience. Enroll all requests identified as constraint-bearing before assignment. Primary endpoint is a paid purchase within 14 days retained through day 45; use 6-8 weeks of enrollment plus maturation, with sample size set from the merchant baseline and minimum worthwhile effect. Guardrails: incompatible recommendations, false exclusions, latency and contribution per shopper.
candidates.metric: ITT difference in retained-purchaser probability: unique assigned shoppers with at least one retained order divided by every eligible assigned shopper. Count all merchant purchases in the category, not just purchases of the promoted candidate. Report AI-referral and merchant-assistant cohorts separately.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase effect. constraint-paper supports technical feasibility; ecom-bench supports a requirement-level offline test design only; constructor-asa and constructor-home establish overlap. No direct conversion percentage is supported.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed traffic or conversion baseline. Chosen sensitivity: GBP40 contribution per additional retained purchaser; GBP600 recurring monthly fee plus operation cost.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even requires 600/40 = 15 additional retained purchasers monthly, or an absolute rate change of 15/N for N eligible monthly shoppers. Add amortized integration costs to the numerator. Zero lift loses GBP600; false exclusions can make the purchase effect negative.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP500/month plus separately quoted integration. Require a paid pilot; no published demand estimate is asserted.
candidates.costControl: Use deterministic predicates after one parse, cache stable compatibility edges and reserve model calls for unresolved language. Never reuse cached stock or price without a valid freshness policy.
dependencies: Accurate category ontology and variant-level source evidence
Enough eligible purchase volume to compare against incumbent search
candidates.failureMode: Bad mappings reject good products, missing specifications create empty results, or an extra verification step adds more friction than it removes.
candidates.falsifier: Reject the claim if a powered test rules out the minimum worthwhile retained-purchase increase, or verified incompatibility/false-exclusion guardrails worsen. Better simulated constraint satisfaction alone does not rescue it.

candidates.title: Ask only the question that can change the purchase decision
candidates.buyer: Retailers of considered purchases whose AI shoppers frequently arrive with incomplete requirements.
candidates.problem: A chatbot can ask many reasonable questions that do not change the candidate set, while failing to ask the one question that prevents a wrong or abandoned purchase.
candidates.mechanism: Selection stage: estimate whether one answer would change the suitable shortlist enough to justify the shopper's effort. A useful clarification should reduce a material mismatch or comparison burden before the shopper leaves.
candidates.intervention: Build a question-selection policy that compares expected decision regret with the predicted cost of an extra turn. Candidate actions include asking one bounded question, showing a small provisional shortlist, or proceeding. Ask only for task-relevant preferences, offer 'not sure', and expose why the answer matters.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Constructor ASA already supports conversational refinement. Research already studies appropriate question selection. This proposal is a narrow policy within those experiences, not a new chatbot category.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A policy trained on randomized real-user responses and retained purchases asks fewer irrelevant questions and produces more retained purchasers than either a fixed questionnaire or unrestricted LLM conversation.
dataNeeded: Pre-question request and current feasible candidate set
Candidate question, answerability and response-time estimates
Logged action probabilities from consented live exploration
Shopper answers, abandonment, paid orders and returns
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible shoppers at their first ambiguous request to decision-value questioning, the existing assistant, or a brief fixed questionnaire. candidates.title: Recover stockouts with an explicit substitute-versus-wait policy
candidates.buyer: Merchants with high variant turnover and AI referrals to products that become unavailable.
candidates.problem: A generic similar-products carousel may miss the requirement that made a shopper choose an unavailable item, or divert a shopper who would have bought the original after a short wait.
candidates.mechanism: Landing and selection stages: identify which properties are essential, then choose between a verified substitute, a genuinely available alternate variant, or a truthful wait option. The policy seeks additional retained shoppers after a stockout while accounting for purchases merely moved forward in time.
candidates.intervention: Build a conditional substitution graph with shopper-visible differences and protected requirements. Use restock uncertainty, explicit deadline, delivered cost and historic accepted substitutions to choose a small recovery set. Preserve the original item and let the shopper explicitly approve any relaxed preference.

candidates.costControl: Precompute proven substitute edges and evaluate only currently available options. Do not spend inference on stockouts with no useful recovery action.

candidates.buyer: Specialist merchants whose shoppers repeatedly hesitate over a fact absent from supplier data.
candidates.problem: A product assistant can retrieve every available document and still lack the decisive fact, such as sleeve opening width or the clearance needed to open a storage unit.

The enabling algorithm creates value only when acquired evidence changes actual retained purchases.
candidates.intervention: Build a value-of-information queue that ranks concrete evidence-acquisition tasks by affected real demand, probability the answer changes a shortlist, uncertainty and acquisition cost. Initial scope excludes safety-critical claims.

candidates.edgeHypothesis: A fixed evidence budget spent on facts that can change a real purchase decision produces more retained purchasers than a catalogue-completeness queue or existing gap scorer.

Auditable measurement results plus assigned-shopper orders and returns

Primary endpoint is category-wide retained purchasers, not resolved questions; check incorrect claims and cross-cluster spillover.

Count unfavorable evidence that correctly disqualifies a product, and do not count successful measurements as sales.

candidates.title: Spend extra reasoning only when it can change a purchase decision
candidates.buyer: High-volume merchants operating a shopping assistant or approved agent tool with noticeable latency and inference cost.
candidates.problem: Uniformly expensive reasoning wastes time on easy requests, while a cheap model can fail on the small subset needing compatibility checks or fresh quotes.
candidates.mechanism: Decision and response stages: route easy, verified requests through a fast path and spend computation on ambiguous high-regret cases. Faster useful answers can prevent abandonment; retained savings can fund more valuable verification. Purchase preservation is a required constraint, not an assumed consequence of lower cost.
candidates.intervention: Build a calibrated decision-stability router using constraint coverage, evidence freshness, model disagreement and price/stock volatility. Actions are a deterministic lookup, a small model, an additional authoritative tool call or a stronger model. Assess whether the final product decision changes, and cap latency. Do not treat model self-confidence as calibrated truth.
candidates.competitorOverlap: FrugalGPT and RouteLLM already study cost-aware cascades and routing. Merchant assistants already choose content sources. The edge hypothesis is a commerce-specific objective and guardrails based on real retained purchases and exact decision errors.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Against both always-expensive reasoning and a simple rule-based router, decision-stability routing maintains or improves retained-purchaser rate while reducing cost and response delay. Savings alone are insufficient if purchases fall.
dataNeeded: Request class and exact evidence/tool state
Outputs, latency and cost from candidate execution paths
Human-verified decision errors on a held-out category set
candidates.experiment: Persistently randomize eligible assistant shoppers to router, always-strong execution or a simple deterministic router. Start after blinded offline decision-error checks. Run 6-8 weeks plus returns, powered for a prespecified purchase noninferiority margin and superiority if faster responses are claimed to increase purchases. Guardrails include factual/compatibility errors, timeout rate and contribution per shopper.
candidates.metric: Primary is retained purchasers divided by every assigned eligible shopper. Cost per retained purchaser and p95 answer latency are secondary. Claim incremental purchases only if the randomized purchase contrast is positive with appropriate uncertainty; otherwise report a bounded cost tradeoff.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized commerce effect. routellm and frugalgpt establish adjacent routing methods, not current-model savings or shopping conversion lift.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed traffic, latency or conversion assumed. Sensitivity uses S for measured monthly inference savings, GBP600/month fee/operations and GBP40 contribution per changed retained purchaser.
impactScenario.calculation: Net contribution = S + 40*delta_retained_purchasers - 600 - amortized_setup. For illustration only, if S=GBP1,000, cost breaks even at delta=-10 before setup; the purchase-preservation guardrail can still reject that loss. With S=0, 15 extra retained purchasers are needed. Zero or negative purchase effects must be reported.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP400/month plus usage, or a capped share of audited savings only after purchase noninferiority is established.
candidates.costControl: This is the cost lever: cached verified lookups, bounded tool calls and selective larger-model use. Reinvest only demonstrable savings into experiments that can generate more purchases.
dependencies: Merchant controls execution and can observe model/tool costs
Enough traffic to detect a meaningful conversion loss
candidates.failureMode: The router is confident on difficult cases, cached facts become stale, or extra routing overhead erases latency savings.
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the router breaches the purchase/error noninferiority limits, or a static two-rule cascade matches its cost and conversion with less complexity.

Explicit shopper task/context without sensitive inference
Exposure probabilities, position and accepted/rejected choices
All-category orders, returns and contribution over the full assignment window

candidates.title: Repair the second failed query without dropping a hard constraint
candidates.buyer: Merchants with complex catalogs and a measurable stream of shoppers arriving from AI shopping or search.
candidates.problem: A shopper repeatedly rewords the same need, gets no valid result, and leaves. Ordinary query expansion can remove the very constraint that made the product hard to find.
candidates.mechanism: Discovery recovery: recognize the failed edit sequence, preserve explicit requirements, resolve one ambiguity, and retrieve a genuinely purchasable match. A useful match can turn an otherwise abandoned AI-origin journey into an order.
candidates.intervention: Add a repair mode after two failed searches or explicit rejection of all results. Show the requirements retained, identify the unresolved distinction, ask at most one necessary question, and rerun against live eligible variants. Keep ordinary search available and record which attempted repair failed.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Algolia already suggests queries; Constructor already supports conversational refinement and catalog validation. The edge is a bounded recovery policy across failed edits. Whether their deployed products already handle this equally well is unknown and requires comparison.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: At the same retrieval quality and latency budget, using the sequence of failed edits will recover more valid purchases than an isolated-query suggestion.
dataNeeded: Consented first-party query and result sequences
Explicit hard requirements and rejection reasons
Verified AI-origin referral or partner session

candidates.metric: Retained purchasers divided by every randomized eligible AI-origin shopper, including those who ignore the prompt; report absolute intention-to-treat difference. Purchases through any later merchant path count. Successful query reformulation is diagnostic only.
candidates.impactEvidence: Adjacent measured purchase evidence: beh-fang supports query refinement, but not this sequence-specific repair or external-AI transfer. Our incremental effect is hypothesized.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured AI-origin baseline. Measure N eligible people per month, control retained-purchase probability p0, contribution m per retained purchase, and all-in incremental monthly cost C.
impactScenario.calculation: For a stable population and contribution mix, extra retained purchasers = N * (pT - pC). Incremental contribution = N * (pT - pC) * m - C. Break-even absolute probability gain = C / (N * m). C includes software, inference, integration amortization and extra human work.
impactScenario.range: No empirical range estimated. Zero and negative effects remain possible; a gain among users who engage cannot replace the effect across all assigned eligible users.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP 300 per merchant per month after a measured purchase pilot; require incremental contribution above the full operating cost.
candidates.costControl: Use deterministic failure triggers and cached catalog constraints before calling a model. Limit the repair to one question; measure whether the cap loses purchases.
candidates.failureMode: The question adds work, misreads a legitimate exploratory search, or silently relaxes a non-negotiable requirement.
candidates.falsifier: No economically useful retained-purchase difference against current query assistance at the preregistered precision, or more requirement violations despite better click rates.

candidates.problem: A shopper alternates between the same two products and repeats a question because the answer does not establish the one fact that determines suitability.

A purchase prevented because the item is unsuitable is not a conversion failure; report return-adjusted contribution and false-pass harm.
impactScenario.range: No empirical range estimated. Zero and negative effects remain possible; a gain among users who engage cannot replace the effect across all assigned eligible users.

candidates.title: Turn a failed purchase trace into a tested repair
candidates.buyer: Commerce engineering teams deciding which agent-origin defects deserve release time.
candidates.problem: A conversion dashboard can show a drop without reproducing the offer version, checkout state, and deployment that caused an individual purchase failure.
candidates.mechanism: Enabling tool: trace-linked deterministic reproduction identifies and validates a specific repair; releasing that repair can increase purchases. Storing traces alone has no conversion effect.
candidates.intervention: Join an opaque experiment/session ID to merchant-controlled offer snapshots, schema version, checkout requests, release SHA, provider receipts, order, and later refund state. Produce a minimized sandbox replay with credentials and personal data removed. Rank only reproducible failures by observed affected checkouts and test a repair in a merchant-controlled randomized release.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Google already has a UCP request/response and latency logger plus purchase analytics; Peec joins GA4, crawl, and prompt information. UCP orders already support reconciliation. The proposed edge is cross-protocol, version-specific incident reproduction and verified repair delivery, not another attribution dashboard.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: An engineering team given a replayable failure and its affected purchase cohort will ship more purchase-generating fixes per engineering week than a team given native logs and dashboards alone.
dataNeeded: Merchant-controlled response snapshots and release identity
Engineering time and reproducible defect taxonomy
candidates.experiment: Randomize matched merchant integration teams to native observability versus trace-to-repair workflow, with equal engineering capacity and an eight-to-twelve-week window. For each candidate repair, randomize eligible AI checkout traffic and measure paid orders within seven days. Primary program endpoint: retained AI-origin orders per assigned merchant-month, adjusted using a pre-period baseline. Power both the merchant-level comparison and nested trials; report null, negative, and uncertain repair effects and avoid summing overlapping effects.
candidates.metric: The outer randomized comparison estimates retained AI-origin orders gained per merchant-month at equal engineering effort. Nested purchase trials explain which repairs contribute; time-to-fix and detection rate are secondary. Uncertain repair estimates are not recoded as proven zero or uplift.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized enabling effect. google-logger, google-analytics, peec-referrals, and ucp-orders establish that many inputs and native alternatives already exist. No incremental purchase percentage is supported.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured fix throughput, incident prevalence, or purchase effect. Let I be the nonoverlapping incremental retained orders from deployed repairs and C total workflow and engineering cost.
impactScenario.calculation: Net value = contribution from I-C. Break-even requires more retained contribution than both software cost and the opportunity cost of diverted engineering time.
impactScenario.range: Zero if dashboards already lead to the same fixes; negative if teams spend time replaying rare faults instead of fixing larger purchase barriers.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP 1,500/month per merchant engineering team, tested against native logging plus existing observability spend.
candidates.costControl: Keep immutable compact envelopes for all transactions, retain full sanitized payloads only for sampled faults, and stop investigating faults with too little plausible purchase value.
dependencies: Sandbox capable of deterministic commerce replay
Engineering ownership to deploy an actual fix
candidates.failureMode: The trace omits the true dependency, records sensitive payment data, or the replay only succeeds because it unrealistically freezes live inventory.
candidates.falsifier: No increase in verified incremental purchases at equal engineering capacity, even if diagnostic dashboards look better.

candidates.title: Preserve units, totals, and cart state across protocol adapters
candidates.buyer: Retailers of measured goods, multipacks, and complex configurations integrating several agent channels.
candidates.problem: A schema-valid adapter can still treat a pack as a unit, convert scaled quantities twice, lose an omitted cart field, or drop a tax/fulfillment condition when crossing protocol and API versions.
candidates.mechanism: Selection validity and checkout completion: retain the buyer's exact intended order across representations, exposing unsupported cases before payment instead of producing a surprise total or failed checkout.
candidates.intervention: Create a typed merchant basket model carrying product and pack identity, exact quantity/unit/scale, currency exponent, tax basis, fulfillment IDs, and revision. Implement version-specific adapters and bidirectional semantic checks against authoritative checkout totals. Treat full-state replacement and patch updates differently. If a target cannot represent an item correctly, use a truthful browser handoff rather than silently coercing it.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Stripe ACS already spans protocols, UCP specifies interoperability, and commerce integrators already map baskets. The edge is verified semantic equivalence for difficult merchandise and migration cases; translating JSON alone is not defensible.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A conformance suite built from real merchant baskets can prevent commercially meaningful silent corruption that schema validation and generic adapters miss.
dataNeeded: ERP sale-unit definitions and pack IDs
Mismatch, order, return, and support outcomes
candidates.experiment: Run generated edge-case baskets and recorded failures through native adapters and the semantic model in a sandbox. On an approved agent integration, randomize eligible complex-basket sessions before mapping to baseline or checked adapters. Primary endpoint: correctly priced paid orders for the buyer's intended quantity within seven days per assigned session. Run six weeks or to powered sample, including at least one planned version migration. Guardrails: no overcharge, unauthorized substitution, or increased wrong-unit returns.
candidates.metric: Intent-to-treat correctly constituted purchase probability, with total paid orders and 30-day returns alongside it. Passing a schema or replay is a release gate, not a purchase outcome.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. ucp-core and shopify-carts document real representation and replacement semantics; stripe-acs demonstrates direct incumbent overlap. Consumer support for each complex case still needs approval.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured complex-basket volume, semantic-error rate, or baseline checkout completion. Let E be affected eligible baskets and r the extra retained purchase probability when their representation is corrected.
impactScenario.calculation: Additional retained purchases = E*r minus losses from extra escalation or mapping delay; require contribution above adapter maintenance and service cost.
impactScenario.range: Zero if products use simple each-unit baskets already handled correctly; negative if strict validation rejects valid carts or sends too many buyers through a longer path.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP 2,000/month for a catalog with demonstrated cross-protocol quantity or totals failures.
candidates.costControl: Use deterministic decimal arithmetic and reusable property checks; keep generative models out of price and quantity conversion.
dependencies: A supported buyer handoff for unrepresentable cases
candidates.failureMode: A supposedly canonical model erases a merchant-specific sale basis, or public protocol support is mistaken for availability on a particular consumer channel.
candidates.falsifier: No material semantic errors beyond native adapters, or corrected representations do not improve retained intended orders.

candidates.title: Bind the selected delivery promise to stock and capacity
candidates.buyer: Retailers with store pickup, local delivery, warehouse cutoffs, or time-sensitive products.
candidates.problem: An agent can recommend an in-stock item with a plausible delivery promise, but the selected warehouse, pickup location, or delivery slot cannot fulfill that promise by the time checkout begins.
candidates.mechanism: Discovery relevance and checkout completion: find a feasible offer for the buyer's declared destination and deadline, preserve its location and method, and revalidate the promise before authorization. Fewer unusable recommendations can become paid, successfully fulfilled orders.
candidates.intervention: Build an authoritative availability-to-promise service combining sellable stock, picking capacity, carrier cutoff, store hours, and merchant service zones. Return a quote tied to exact item/location/method and a bounded expiry; where the merchant supports it, reserve capacity only after explicit checkout intent. Carry the same location and option IDs into supported agent checkout or web fallback, and visibly re-quote after expiry.
candidates.competitorOverlap: UCP already models catalog and checkout fulfillment, native platforms calculate delivery choices, and OMS vendors offer availability-to-promise. The proposed edge is continuity between the agent's selected promise and the merchant's capacity commitment, not displaying shipping text.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: For deadline-sensitive purchases, preserving a feasible location-and-capacity choice will outperform global stock plus a fresh generic checkout delivery estimate.
dataNeeded: Paid orders, promised delivery, actual fulfillment, and cancellations
candidates.experiment: Use cooperating agents with supported fulfillment capabilities. Randomize shoppers before feasible-offer selection, or randomize separate destination/capacity pools where reservations could interfere. Compare normal merchant delivery selection with promise continuity for six-to-eight weeks, including cutoff boundaries. Primary endpoint: paid orders fulfilled by the buyer's declared deadline per assigned eligible shopper; also report paid orders alone. Follow failures and cancellations through delivery. Power from pool-level variance.
candidates.metric: Intent-to-treat on-time paid purchase probability across all assigned shoppers, including those shown no feasible offer. Total retained contribution across all capacity-sharing channels guards against shifting scarce slots.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. ucp-fulfillment specifies transportable fulfillment data and google-faq assigns address/inventory responsibility to merchants. Neither proves a capacity hold or a conversion uplift.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured deadline-sensitive traffic, failed promises, or capacity displacement. Let R be extra paid on-time orders and D orders displaced elsewhere.
impactScenario.calculation: Net additional successful purchases = R-D; compare retained contribution after extra fulfillment cost with integration and service cost.
impactScenario.range: Zero when promises are already reliable; negative if overly conservative estimates suppress demand or expensive routing erases margin.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP 2,000/month for a regional retailer with measured delivery-promise failures.
candidates.costControl: Reuse OMS and carrier calculators, invalidate only affected locations/cutoffs, and spend capacity checks on deadline-sensitive shopping intents.
dependencies: Supported capability on the selected agent channel
Operational authority to reserve and honor a promise
candidates.failureMode: The merchant cannot commit capacity, pickup and shipping location semantics are confused, or the engine ignores the returned fulfillment context.
candidates.falsifier: More accurate promises produce no additional paid on-time orders, or gains are offset by displacement and fulfillment costs.

candidates.title: Admit verified shopping agents without opening the whole store
candidates.buyer: Merchants whose WAF or bot controls block legitimate AI product retrieval or buyer-directed checkout.
candidates.problem: A blanket bot challenge can stop a real shopping agent before product selection or checkout, while broadly allowing an AI-looking user-agent permits abuse and stock hoarding.
candidates.mechanism: Access and purchase completion: authenticate a real permitted agent, allow the exact approved read or checkout operation, and retain normal transaction authorization. Incremental sales require previously blocked legitimate shopping demand.
candidates.intervention: Provide a merchant-owned access policy adapter using supported bot verification and platform credentials. Separate product reads from customer or checkout writes, enforce route-level scope, short expiry, rate limits, and merchant-side replay/idempotency handling. Test signed and unsigned requests on merchant-controlled endpoints. Use verified identity as one policy input, never as permission to charge.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Cloudflare already verifies bot/agent identity and lets merchants configure access; platform authentication already exists. The edge is a tested commerce route policy with a measured purchase effect and matched abuse guardrails, not inventing agent signatures or defeating bot controls.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Narrow commerce policies will recover agent-origin purchases lost to overbroad challenges without the fraud and operational cost of a general allow rule.
dataNeeded: Verified agent identity and permitted scopes
Abuse, origin load, and stock-hold metrics
candidates.experiment: First validate policies in shadow mode and merchant-owned sandbox traffic. Randomize allowed partner shopping sessions to the existing merchant policy or narrowly scoped admission where assignment before the challenge is possible; otherwise randomize merchants or matched route/catalog clusters and allow crawl wash-in. Run at least six weeks and to a powered sample. Primary endpoint: paid retained AI-origin orders per assigned partner session or merchant-day. Stop for elevated unauthorized writes, fraud, or origin exhaustion.
candidates.metric: Intent-to-treat retained purchases including initially challenged sessions. Bot requests, challenge pass rate, and page fetches are diagnostic; absent proof of buyer-driven origin, request counts are not shopper counts.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. cloudflare-auth and cloudflare-verified document identification mechanisms and limits; google-faq supports authenticating platform requests rather than assuming request geography.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured legitimate blocked shopping volume, baseline purchases, or abuse cost. Let B be blocked legitimate shopping sessions, r added retained purchase probability, and L added fraud/operational loss.
impactScenario.calculation: Net value = B*r*retained-order contribution-L-service cost; recovery must exceed both software cost and any new abuse loss.
impactScenario.range: Zero if legitimate shopping agents are already admitted; negative if identity is treated as authorization or added access mostly serves non-buying automation.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: GBP 750/month per storefront with confirmed legitimate shopping blocks.
candidates.costControl: Use existing edge verification, evaluate simple deterministic policies, and log expensive details only for policy mismatches and incidents.
dependencies: Real agent verification supported by the provider
An experiment unit identifiable before policy execution
candidates.failureMode: A valid signature is replayed or overtrusted; an agent passes identity checks without buyer purchase authority; measured requests cannot be connected to purchases.
candidates.falsifier: Admission increases bot traffic but not retained purchases, or fraud and infrastructure costs exceed recovered contribution.

candidates.title: Recover destination-rejected baskets with a lawful local offer
candidates.buyer: Cross-border merchants and distributors whose AI-originated buyers hit unsupported destinations or product restrictions.
candidates.problem: A shopping assistant can select the right model from an offer that the buyer cannot receive. A product ban, a platform restriction, an unavailable carrier and a missing address are different failures, yet each can end the purchase.
candidates.mechanism: Selection and checkout. Determine the actual failure before recommending; when a permitted same-model local-stock offer exists, present it with the real seller and destination terms. Fewer dead ends may produce additional completed orders rather than wasted product clicks.
candidates.intervention: Connect the merchant's approved SKU-by-destination rules, carrier acceptance and stock to a resolver that returns allowed, unavailable or needs-review with evidence timestamps. Where authorized distribution partners agree, resolve a permitted local offer and preserve the chosen variant in its checkout. Request the intended delivery destination; never infer nationality or bypass a restriction.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify Managed Markets already restricts and hides products by market and supports re-review [markets]. Shopify has agent carts and continue_url [cart]. The proposed gap is reason-specific recovery into another permitted offer. No absence of equivalent partner routing is established.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A network of local sellers plus auditable rule reasons recovers purchases that simple hiding loses. Its advantage should be greatest where identical models have different stock locations and commercial delivery coverage.
dataNeeded: Merchant-approved destination/category policy with source and review date
Carrier and platform restriction reasons separate from legal status
Local partner stock, price, delivery and order/refund feeds
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible AI-originated shoppers before destination resolution, keeping the current lawful restrictions in both arms. Compare existing platform-supported availability UX with the optional local-offer recovery. Measure paid orders retained 45 days across participating sellers. Run at least eight weeks, then mature returns; power from observed failure prevalence and baseline, not a fixed promised lift. Guard against restricted sales, destination errors, silent seller swaps and extra fees.
candidates.metric: Retained orders per all randomized destination-query shoppers, including those for whom no route exists. Report merchant share separately from network-wide additional purchases; a seller switch alone is not incremental demand.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. [markets] establishes a real restriction workflow; [geo] distinguishes delivery area from nationality; [gpsr] establishes relevant EU offer information. No causal purchase effect found for this proposed routing extension.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed traffic or conversion baseline. Choose EUR 600 monthly fee and EUR 40 contribution per additional retained order only for a break-even test.
impactScenario.calculation: 600 / 40 = 15 additional retained orders per month before integration costs. With onboarding cost I amortized over H months, threshold is (600 + I/H) / 40.
impactScenario.range: Unknown. Zero or negative effects are possible if no permitted alternative exists, routing adds friction, or orders merely move between sellers.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test price: EUR 600 per month for one origin/destination corridor; require contribution-based payback after returns and partner fees.
candidates.costControl: Reuse platform restriction states and cache unchanged source rules. Pay for human review only on high-intent ambiguous SKU/destination pairs; never resolve uncertainty by making a sale.
dependencies: A merchant compliance owner for country/product decisions
Native commerce access and carrier integrations
Clear offer ownership and lawful data sharing
candidates.failureMode: A stale permission or misleading local-seller substitution creates unfulfillable orders. Blanket residence filtering may conflict with EU geo-blocking protections.
candidates.falsifier: No meaningful recoverable permitted-offer population, or an adequately powered test produces no additional retained network purchases after margin and cancellation costs.
