candidates.title: Carry a verified discount entitlement through the agent handoff
candidates.buyer: Merchants running genuine student or professional discount programs that rely on third-party verification.
candidates.problem: A shopper qualifies for a gated offer, but crossing from an assistant to a merchant checkout loses the verification result or triggers another document request.
candidates.mechanism: Checkout eligibility. Reuse a short-lived, merchant-accepted proof for the same offer so a qualified customer sees and redeems the promised price without another verification loop.
candidates.intervention: Create an offer-scoped proof exchange between an existing verification provider, a participating assistant and the merchant's discount extension. Bind proof to offer, expiry, audience and redemption limits; accept only issuer-approved claims, not an assistant's self-asserted status. Keep raw identity documents with the verifier. Always retain the normal verification path.
candidates.competitorOverlap: SheerID already verifies eligibility and integrates gated offers [sheerid]. Shopify already supports discounts and agent checkout, but documents that WebMCP does not cover app-defined checkout extension interactions [cart]. W3C credentials supply an existing representation, not merchant trust [vc].
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Bridging a specific verification extension produces fewer legitimate redemption failures than adding a generic wallet or another discount code. Cross-merchant reuse is valuable only when each merchant explicitly trusts the issuer and the claim scope.
dataNeeded: Issuer authorization, expiry and revocation/status mechanisms
Verification failure reasons and order-level fraud, discount and refund outcomes
candidates.experiment: Randomize shoppers when they request an eligible offer, before verification succeeds. Control uses the merchant's existing verification flow; treatment offers accepted proof reuse and the same fallback. Hold discount amount, products and expiry constant. Primary endpoint is retained paid orders per assigned shopper after 45 days. Run eight weeks plus maturation; calculate power from actual repeat-verification incidence. Guardrails include unauthorized redemptions, false refusals and identity disclosure.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat retained purchase rate among everyone requesting the offer, including failed checks. Report saved verification steps separately; do not compare successful verifiers with unverified users.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. [sheerid], [cart] and [vc] support the workflow and implementation boundary. No measured incremental purchase result for this handoff adapter was located.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured funnel baseline. Choose EUR 400 monthly fee and EUR 25 contribution per retained order after discount and fraud cost.
impactScenario.calculation: 400 / 25 = 16 extra retained orders per month; add provider verification fees and integration amortization before declaring payback.
impactScenario.range: Unknown; zero if repeat verification is rare, negative if proof reuse causes fraud or its extra consent step deters buyers.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: EUR 400 per month plus disclosed provider usage, tested against recovered contribution rather than gross discounted revenue.
candidates.costControl: Use established verification providers and reuse only unexpired authorized proofs. Avoid building document verification or retaining raw documents.
dependencies: Appropriate consent and lawful-basis design for each processing purpose
candidates.failureMode: A credential format is mistaken for trusted eligibility, or a broad reusable identifier enables tracking across merchants. The extra proof UX may be slower than a working native flow.
candidates.falsifier: The native verifier already preserves eligibility reliably, or reuse fails to increase retained orders without unacceptable unauthorized discounts.

candidates.title: Bind the recommended seller to verifiable product provenance
candidates.buyer: Brands and authorized specialist retailers competing with visually identical offers whose seller or product provenance is unclear.
candidates.problem: An assistant merges product evidence across sellers. The buyer sees a known model and assumes every linked offer has the same origin, support and condition, then hesitates or purchases from an unsuitable seller.
candidates.mechanism: Selection and retailer choice. Present evidence tied to the exact seller/model offer, then preserve that identity through checkout. Reduced uncertainty may recover purchases from buyers who would otherwise abstain.
candidates.intervention: Build a revocable brand-to-seller attestation for a scoped range of models and dates, plus exact GTIN/model matching and verified seller contact details. Offer a plain evidence view stating what was checked and what remains unknown. Where genuine serial or lot evidence exists, link it without treating a barcode match as physical authentication. Apply known recall blocks to every arm.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Verified by GS1 already resolves identifier ownership [gs1], and Digital Link connects product IDs to information [digital-link]. GPSR already requires certain offer details [gpsr]. The extension is brand-confirmed seller scope plus preservation of that proof across AI recommendation and cart; other authentication platforms may already supply it.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Exact seller provenance matters more than another product-level trust badge when the same model appears through many retailers. Brand attestations should resolve ambiguity without excluding lawful independent resellers by default.
dataNeeded: Brand-issued seller attestations and withdrawal dates
Current seller identity and support terms
Recall feeds and lot scope where available
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible AI-originated shoppers viewing identical-model offers between the lawful current offer information and the scoped evidence view. Keep price, stock and ranking fixed. Primary endpoint is any retained network purchase after 45 days, with authorized-merchant share secondary. Run eight weeks plus returns; power around measured provenance-related hesitation. Never show recalled inventory or fabricate missing evidence.
candidates.metric: Retained purchases per randomized shopper, plus seller-mismatch and authenticity-related return rates. Attribute seller shifts separately from recovered category purchases.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. [gs1] and [digital-link] support identity infrastructure; [gpsr] supports offer-information obligations. No source establishes a conversion effect for this attestation design.

impactScenario.baseline: No observed conversion or authenticity-failure baseline. Choose EUR 800 monthly brand-network fee and EUR 50 contribution per extra retained network order.
impactScenario.calculation: 800 / 50 = 16 additional retained orders per month, excluding issuance and investigation costs.
impactScenario.range: Unknown. Zero if consumers already trust the seller; negative if ambiguous evidence is presented as suspicion or lawful resellers are wrongly excluded.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: EUR 800 monthly for one brand and a bounded seller network. Charge for measured recovered demand, not a badge sold as certification.
candidates.costControl: Verify seller relationships once per scope/expiry and use revocation events. Do not repeatedly call a model to re-interpret unchanged attestations.
dependencies: A clear distinction between authorization, authenticity, condition and safety
candidates.failureMode: A stolen or overbroad attestation becomes false reassurance. A lack of attestation is incorrectly described as counterfeit or illegal.
candidates.falsifier: The evidence view changes seller allocation but does not increase retained purchases or reduce material mismatches, or brands will not supply credible attestations.

candidates.title: Turn an approved PPE specification into an evidence-complete order
candidates.buyer: Workwear distributors serving small business buyers with an already approved equipment specification.
candidates.problem: A purchaser knows the required standard, version, performance code and size, but must cross-check PDFs and ask support before ordering. Search often treats related standard names as interchangeable.
candidates.mechanism: Qualification and checkout. Match exact user-supplied requirements to model-specific evidence, available sizes and quantities; a purchase that would wait for a manual document exchange can proceed with its evidence packet.
candidates.intervention: Create a deterministic requirement matcher over distributor-approved declarations and product records. It returns satisfied, contradicted or not established for each supplied requirement, with exact document/model/version links, then builds the matching order and purchasing evidence packet. A competent person must set the worksite requirement; the system does not perform the hazard assessment or certify PPE.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Manufacturers such as uvex already publish standards, performance codes and conformity documents [uvex]. The EU PPE declaration is established infrastructure [ppe]. The hypothesized extension is a multi-brand, inventory-aware evidence packet matched to a purchaser's approved requirement, not standards-name extraction.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Eliminating model/version ambiguity and support waits helps buyers with known requirements complete purchases. It can also make documented equivalent products saleable when the first choice is out of stock.
dataNeeded: Model-specific current declarations and manufacturer instructions
Structured performance codes without conflating standard versions
Size/quantity inventory and procurement order outcomes
candidates.experiment: Randomize purchasing accounts before their first specification lookup; compare normal distributor search/document access with the evidence-complete matcher. Apply the same product/safety restrictions and human escalation in both arms. Primary endpoint is paid orders whose selected models match the supplied documentary requirements, retained after 60 days per account. This is a document match, not a safety assurance. Run twelve weeks or the power-derived procurement cycle. Guardrails include document mismatch, unsafe substitutions and incorrect requirement interpretation.
candidates.metric: Retained order rate per randomized account and time from specification entry to paid order. Count a bundled purchase once; report line-item units separately.

candidates.title: Let the shopper edit the recommendation's assumptions
candidates.buyer: Electronics and hobby-equipment merchants receiving AI-assisted comparison traffic.
candidates.problem: A recommendation can be factually accurate but depend on an unstated assumption, such as valuing portability over repairability. The shopper rejects the recommendation without being able to correct that assumption.
candidates.mechanism: Selection and purchase: visible control over decision assumptions may make the recommendation usable, while substantive corrections improve product fit. More suitable purchases must survive returns; increased obedience alone is not the objective.
candidates.intervention: On the merchant's assistant or comparison page, show the three assumptions in its own recommendation model that actually change the recommended SKU. Let the shopper replace one, mark it unknown, or veto it. Recompute the shortlist and identify the consequential change. A referral does not reveal the outside AI's hidden reasoning; requirements must come from explicit shopper input or data the merchant actually has. Keep full-catalog access and prices.
candidates.competitorOverlap: ChatGPT shopping research already accepts preference feedback; Constructor supports conversational refinement; Zoovu offers guided buying. The proposed difference is an inspectable, editable assumption-to-SKU dependency, not another conversation box. Equivalent vendor functionality may exist and needs a demo comparison.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: For explicitly uncertain shoppers, correcting a consequential assumption produces more retained purchases than asking another broad preference question.
dataNeeded: Referred SKU or voluntary shortlist and requirements; no assumed access to an external chat
Recomputation trace linking changed assumptions to different eligible products
Persistent assignment, orders, refunds and contribution
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible unique human AI referrals before first exposure, with assignment persisting across sessions. Compare standard conversational clarification with the editable-assumption panel using the same catalog and recommendation engine. Primary endpoint is any completed purchase retained through the standard return window within 30 days of assignment. Accrue for at least six weeks and extend to the preregistered sample required by merchant baseline and minimum meaningful effect; mature returns afterward. Guardrails: factual accuracy, hard-budget violations, returns, latency and decision effort.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat difference in retained purchasers divided by all randomized eligible humans, with total-catalog orders and net contribution as checks. Do not compare editors with non-editors or call this an AI acquisition effect.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase effect. alg-edit provides adjacent human forecasting evidence: control over forecasts increased algorithm use, not ecommerce purchasing. No transfer percentage is defensible.

impactScenario.baseline: Chosen monthly assumptions only: N=10000 eligible unique humans, retained-purchase rate 2%, contribution GBP 40 per additional retained order. None is an observed merchant baseline.
impactScenario.calculation: Monthly fee GBP 500 plus GBP 0.02 per eligible visitor at rollout costs GBP 700. Break-even requires 17.5 additional retained orders, or 0.175 percentage points of retained-purchase rate, assuming one order per additional purchaser and unchanged basket mix. impactScenario.range: Unknown; zero or negative effects are plausible if the flow creates work or surfaces irreconcilable conflict.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated merchant pilot price: GBP 750/month for a high-consideration joint-purchase category.
candidates.costControl: Use deterministic constraint intersections and a limited explanatory model call. Keep preference storage short-lived and avoid a general social network.
candidates.failureMode: Invitations add friction, privacy expectations are violated, or structured negotiation intensifies disagreement rather than resolving it.
candidates.falsifier: After sufficient independent groups and purchase maturation, the trial excludes the minimum useful retained-purchase gain or privacy/conflict guardrails fail.

candidates.title: Test an honest 'keep what you have' recommendation
candidates.buyer: Repeat-purchase merchants with enough customer continuity to measure whether credible advice earns future business.
candidates.problem: A buyer suspects every assistant answer will lead to a new sale, even when their existing product already meets the stated need. That suspicion can weaken later recommendations.
candidates.mechanism: Long-horizon confidence to future retained purchases: a truthful outside option may make later useful recommendations more credible. Immediate sales can fall; the proposal is viable only if cumulative incremental retained purchases and contribution eventually increase.
candidates.intervention: Where verified facts show the existing product meets every stated requirement, display a 'keep what you have' option beside relevant replacements, with the exact reason and a clear condition that would justify upgrading. A shopper may ignore it. Use only voluntarily supplied ownership information. Do not invent a deficiency to create a later upsell or send follow-up marketing without permission.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Conversational assistants can already discuss tradeoffs and alternatives; a do-nothing option is not technically novel. The proposed edge is a merchant incentive and evaluation contract that allows honest abstention and tests cumulative retained purchases. No claim is made that competitors always push purchases.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: In a repeat-shopping category, demonstrably useful advice when no purchase is needed increases later voluntary use and sufficiently many retained purchases to offset foregone immediate sales.
dataNeeded: All catalog orders, returns, incentives and contribution for at least 180 days
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible consenting customers, persistently, between current accurate product advice and the same advice with an explicit factual outside option. Never conceal essential fit limitations in the control. Primary endpoint: cumulative retained order count per assigned customer over 180 days, followed by return maturation; retain a 365-day exploratory holdout if feasible. Size the test for an economically meaningful long-horizon difference and account for attrition. Guardrails: immediate and cumulative contribution, inappropriate upsells, consent and data deletion.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat difference in cumulative retained orders/all randomized customers. Voluntary return visits and trust ratings are mediators. Reduced returns, lower costs, or shifting purchases later without more cumulative retained orders cannot alone satisfy this purchase objective.
candidates.impactEvidence: Frontier hypothesis with no direct retained-purchase evidence found. two-sided concerns credibility and conditional persuasion, not proof that advising against a purchase creates future orders. This is a reserve experiment, not a launch claim.

impactScenario.baseline: Chosen six-month cohort: 10,000 eligible customers, 0.15 retained orders per customer over 180 days, GBP 40 contribution per incremental retained order. These are invented planning assumptions.
impactScenario.calculation: Six months at GBP 500/month plus GBP 0.03 per eligible customer costs GBP 3,300. Break-even requires 82.5 more cumulative retained orders, or +0.00825 retained orders per customer, after counting any immediate orders forgone. This is not a predicted loyalty lift.
impactScenario.range: Unknown, with a substantial negative possibility. If cumulative orders fall, the idea fails the stated objective even when customers prefer the advice.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 500/month only for a merchant willing to maintain the long holdout; a short-term conversion buyer is a poor fit.
candidates.costControl: Start with narrow, verifiable upgrade rules rather than a broad ownership graph. Stop expansion until the long-horizon purchase signal justifies it.
dependencies: Commercial willingness to accept honest abstention
candidates.failureMode: Foregone sales never return, customers buy from competitors, or a truthful no-buy message is received as dismissive rather than useful.
candidates.falsifier: The prespecified long-horizon trial rules out an economically useful increase in cumulative retained orders, or the effect exists only in stated trust with no purchase consequence.

candidates.title: Route each stated arrival deadline to a deliverable offer
candidates.buyer: Gift, travel and event-goods merchants with meaningful delivery-deadline demand.
candidates.problem: A product can meet every specification yet arrive after the shopper needs it; a generic delivery estimate leaves that mismatch unresolved.
candidates.mechanism: Selection and checkout: preserve the shopper's need-by date, resolve the actual warehouse, cutoff and service, and offer only credible delivery or collection paths. More feasible paths could produce additional paid orders; a stricter filter could also reduce them.
candidates.intervention: A merchant-owned deadline resolver consumes postcode, timestamp, chosen variant and need-by date; returns dated delivery options, source timestamps and the last real order cutoff; carries the selected service into checkout and rechecks it there. No unsupported guaranteed-arrival language.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Google Merchant Center already models delivery dates and cutoff times. Existing carrier and merchant checkout estimates are the comparator. The hypothesis is preserving a shopper-specific deadline through AI selection and handoff; no universal competitor absence is claimed.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: An explicit feasibility check and a valid fallback such as collection can recover deadline-sensitive purchases that truthful generic estimates lose.
dataNeeded: User-supplied deadline and coarse delivery location
Warehouse and carrier calendars, cutoff and holidays
Variant inventory and checkout shipping quotes
Observed on-time delivery and retained orders
candidates.experiment: Randomize identifiable AI-origin buyers after collecting the same optional deadline in both arms. Compare current accurate estimates with resolved deadline options. Primary endpoint is a paid order retained after the return window per eligible buyer; on-time receipt is a guardrail. Run across weekday, weekend and cutoff boundaries for at least six weeks, then mature outcomes; power from observed baseline and deadline prevalence. Do not falsify control estimates.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat retained purchase probability among all preidentified deadline-bearing AI-origin buyers. Report order count, late-delivery rate and incremental contribution; this on-site test does not establish discovery lift.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase effect; google-delivery and google-cutoff establish existing operational inputs, not a conversion percentage.

impactScenario.baseline: Unmeasured N eligible AI-origin deadline shoppers, control retained-purchase rate c0, deadline-failure prevalence f and contribution m. No baseline is assumed positive.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental retained orders = N*(cT-c0). Break-even requires N*(cT-c0)*m to exceed fee plus incremental shipping, integration and support cost. Zero or negative change is possible, especially if current estimates already solve the problem.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 300 per store per month plus a separately quoted integration. Renewal requires measured incremental contribution above total cost.
candidates.costControl: Use deterministic calendars and cached carrier routes; refresh near actual cutoff changes and checkout. Reserve model calls for interpreting user-supplied dates.
dependencies: Merchant or approved agent interface able to receive a deadline
candidates.failureMode: Overconfident estimates create late orders; conservative estimates suppress viable ones; most shoppers never supply a date.
candidates.falsifier: A powered test rules out the merchant's predeclared break-even retained-order effect, or any gain is erased by late-delivery refunds.

candidates.title: Sell availability for the whole usage interval
candidates.buyer: Equipment, clothing and event-supply rental merchants selling paid bookings online.
candidates.problem: Static in-stock answers cannot tell a shopper whether equipment is available throughout a wedding, trip or production period.
candidates.mechanism: Discovery and selection: bind a shopper's start and end dates to inventory that is actually bookable throughout that interval, then preserve dates into payment. Fewer dead-end calendar checks could yield more paid rental orders.
candidates.intervention: An interval-aware merchant search endpoint checks location, requested quantity, turnaround buffers and start/end times; returns valid rental offers and permitted date alternatives. Carry a signed selection into booking checkout and revalidate before payment.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Booqable already exposes date-aware availability and exact-period inventory quantities. Rebuilding its calendar is not an edge. The proposal connects an AI-origin request to existing bookable inventory without losing its dates.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Calendar constraints preserved from conversation through booking outperform generic product links followed by repeated date entry.
dataNeeded: Explicit rental dates, quantities and location
Live availability API and final price
Paid booking, cancellation and completed rental records
candidates.experiment: Randomize AI-origin date-bearing buyer requests between current product landing pages and interval-preserving results. Endpoint is a paid booking completed without cancellation per randomized request. Follow through rental completion and refund maturity; recruit for at least eight weeks but extend for sufficient independent buyers and seasonal coverage. Monitor wrong-date bookings, double booking and total all-channel orders.
candidates.metric: Completed paid rental orders divided by all randomized eligible requests, with revenue and margin secondary. These are purchases of a rental service; report separately if the portfolio requires only ownership purchases.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; booqable-api proves availability infrastructure and substantial adjacent overlap, not AI-origin purchase lift.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown N eligible rental intents, baseline completed-booking probability b0, calendar-conflict rate f and margin m.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental completed bookings = N*(bT-b0). Value = that difference*m minus integration, refunds and booking cost. It can be zero or negative if native date selection is already easy.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 200 per rental location per month, conditional on net booking contribution exceeding cost.
candidates.costControl: Batch interval checks for shortlisted items and reuse the rental system's calculations. Do not rebuild the inventory calendar in an LLM.
dependencies: An approved AI commerce route or merchant assistant
Booking checkout that preserves interval identity
candidates.failureMode: Availability races or buffer errors double-book stock; rental commerce may fall outside the intended target market.
candidates.falsifier: No incremental completed paid bookings versus the native date-aware flow after adequate power, or additional cancellations absorb the gain.

candidates.title: Match preorder commitment to the shopper's purchase horizon
candidates.buyer: Made-to-order furniture, collectible and limited-production merchants with reliable future supply dates.
candidates.problem: An unavailable item is often treated as a dead end even when the shopper would accept later delivery; conversely, a preorder can be wrong for an urgent need.
candidates.mechanism: Selection and order completion: a declared latest acceptable date determines whether an existing preorder option is suitable. A clear commitment path may convert long-horizon demand while avoiding misleading immediate-availability promises.
candidates.intervention: Expose authoritative preorder status, earliest/latest estimated fulfillment, payment milestones and cancellation terms. An AI or landing module matches them to the shopper's horizon and offers the merchant's current preorder checkout only when suitable. Later date changes trigger only agreed status updates.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify already supports preorder apps with full, partial or no initial payment. OpenAI supports preorder date metadata without implying stock change or date display. The proposed distinction is verified horizon matching and completed-order measurement.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Qualifying the delivery horizon before proposing a preorder will generate more fulfilled, fully paid orders than a generic sold-out or preorder page.
candidates.experiment: Randomize eligible long-horizon AI-origin buyers to existing truthful product/preorder presentation or horizon-matched presentation. Count fully paid, fulfilled and retained orders, not deposits or waitlist registrations. Follow until the release cycle plus return window, which may require several months; stratify by release cohort and predeclare power. No treatment may imply guaranteed supply.
candidates.metric: Retained fulfilled orders per randomized eligible buyer by a common, preregistered horizon. Publish deposits, payment failures and delays separately; these are not purchases in the primary endpoint.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; shopify-preorder and openai-dates support technical feasibility and its limits. No measured effect is available.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown eligible N, control completed-order rate c0, preorder delay/cancellation prevalence and margin m.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental completed orders = N*(cT-c0), evaluated after final payment and fulfillment. Any deposit revenue is excluded until earned. Break-even includes delay support, cancellations and financing cost; zero or negative is possible.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 250 per merchant per month during an eligible release cycle; judge value after completion, not on preorder cash collected.
candidates.costControl: Reuse established preorder apps and event updates. Check unstable supplier milestones more often than fixed, confirmed releases.
candidates.failureMode: Supplier estimates are unreliable, delayed-payment failure dominates, or simpler restock alerts convert equally well.
candidates.falsifier: Apparent preorder gains disappear when counting fulfilled retained orders or when delayed control purchases mature.

candidates.title: Keep a saved shopping need alive only until its own expiry
candidates.buyer: Fashion, outdoor and home merchants whose customers often wait for a qualifying product.
candidates.problem: A back-in-stock alert preserves one SKU but may forget the shopper's delivery deadline, price ceiling, alternative choices or whether the need still exists.
candidates.mechanism: Return visit and purchase: with express permission, retain the shopper's constraints and notify only when a currently purchasable offer satisfies them before the need expires. This may recover an otherwise abandoned AI-origin journey.
candidates.intervention: A saved-intent record contains allowed products/substitutes, size, budget, need-by date, channel permission and delete date. Requalify every outbound offer against stock, total price and arrival feasibility; stop on purchase, expiry or withdrawal. Use a checkout continuation link after a fresh check.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Klaviyo provides stock alerts; its documented flow cannot recheck stock before a second message after the first alert. Shopify provides persistent agent carts. The hypothesis is the compound, expiring qualification rule, not reminders or cart persistence alone.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Rechecking the full need before every authorized notification outperforms ordinary stock alerts and avoids offers that became unsuitable while the shopper waited.
dataNeeded: Explicit saved constraints and channel-specific consent
Live inventory, price and fulfillment facts
candidates.experiment: Randomize consenting AI-origin shoppers with a saved need between their current stock-alert workflow and compound qualification, keeping contact caps equal. Primary endpoint is any qualifying retained purchase by the declared expiry plus returns maturity. Use at least eight weeks of enrollment and enough independent needs for power. Record no-message decisions, false qualifying alerts and unsubscribes.
candidates.metric: Retained purchases of any permitted item per all randomized saved needs, including those receiving no message. A reopened email is not a conversion. Deduplicate one customer need across devices where consent permits.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; klaviyo-backstock establishes adjacent functionality and a scoped limitation; shopify-carts establishes continuity competition; ico-email informs permission design.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown number N of consented AI-origin needs, baseline retained purchase probability p0, qualifying-offer frequency q and contribution m.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental retained purchases = N*(pT-p0), not messages_sent*click_rate. Value subtracts communication and integration cost; zero/negative is plausible if filtering reduces useful reminders or extra consent friction dominates.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 150 per store per month plus transparent message costs; merchant requires incremental contribution above its existing alert system.
candidates.costControl: Evaluate deterministic constraints on inventory/price events, not repeated full-catalog model sweeps. Expire data and stop processing when the need ends.
dependencies: Commercial APIs permitted for background operation
candidates.failureMode: The saved intent becomes stale, a user buys elsewhere, or the extra form discourages completion.
candidates.falsifier: No retained-purchase gain against the existing alert tool after accounting for consent take-up, or false qualifying alerts/complaints rise.

candidates.title: Match gift dates to the actual return window
candidates.buyer: Gift, apparel and consumer-electronics merchants with seasonal or product-specific return policies.
candidates.problem: A shopper may buy a gift early but discover that its return window ends before the recipient opens it; a generic number of return days hides the timing problem.
candidates.mechanism: Selection and confidence: calculate return eligibility against the delivery and gift dates so buyers can choose a suitable item or order time. Reducing uncertainty may yield retained purchases, though honest ineligibility can suppress unsuitable orders.
candidates.intervention: A policy-date calculator resolves SKU exceptions, delivery-based start rules and genuine seasonal overrides. It displays the latest date under the merchant's policy and whether the stated gift date leaves the buyer's requested inspection period. Publish only supported policy fields; link the governing terms.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Google supports merchant return data and seasonal overrides. Shop agents already answer return-policy/window questions. The hypothesis is event-date arithmetic and SKU-specific exceptions carried into selection, not a policy extractor.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: An exact gift-date fit answer resolves a material objection more effectively than a general return-policy link or generic assistant response.
dataNeeded: Optional gift date and desired inspection time
Approved, versioned return policies and SKU exclusions
Delivery estimate or actual delivery date
Retained orders, returns and policy disputes
candidates.experiment: Randomize preidentified AI-origin gift shoppers between accurate current policy presentation and the date calculator. Keep policy generosity identical. Primary retained orders per randomized shopper after the longest applicable policy window; also report initial orders and return costs. Run across a gift season and mature outcomes; power on gift-intent prevalence, not total traffic.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat retained purchase probability in the AI-origin gift cohort. Attribute no separate lift to policy extension unless that is independently randomized.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; google-return and shop-personal establish direct adjacent functionality. No causal gift-date conversion result is claimed.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown N eligible gift shoppers, control retained conversion c0, date-policy mismatch prevalence f and contribution m.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental retained orders = N*(cT-c0). Break-even includes support and return costs. Zero/negative is possible when truthful date calculations reveal ineligibility or generic policies were already understood.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated seasonal pilot: GBP 200 per store per month; renewal depends on retained contribution rather than initial holiday orders.
candidates.costControl: Use a deterministic policy rules engine and versioned merchant approval. Ask for a date only when a gift purpose is explicitly supplied.
dependencies: Clear separation of discretionary merchant policy and statutory rights
Outcome follow-up beyond seasonal return deadlines
candidates.failureMode: Ambiguous exceptions generate false assurances; calculating expected delivery as certain produces incorrect deadlines.
candidates.falsifier: The calculator fails merchant policy review on meaningful cases, or a powered test rules out the prespecified retained-order break-even effect.

candidates.title: Match intended use dates to remaining usable life
candidates.buyer: Fresh-food, celebration-food and other dated perishable-goods merchants.
candidates.problem: Availability and delivery date do not establish that a delivered product will still be suitable when the shopper plans to use it.
candidates.mechanism: Selection and basket completion: show offers whose verified remaining life covers the shopper's use date and stated storage conditions. This can make a dated event basket purchasable and avoid quality-related cancellations.
candidates.intervention: Join the intended use date with warehouse batch allocation or an enforceable minimum-life promise at delivery. Distinguish use-by from best-before; surface qualifying pack sizes and delivery slots. Revalidate at allocation and offer a truthful alternative when the promise cannot be met.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Ocado already publishes a minimum-life Fresh+ Promise. Food-date guidance already distinguishes safety and quality labels. The hypothesis is matching a customer's planned use date to an allocatable batch throughout AI selection and fulfillment.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Event-specific usable-life qualification removes uncertainty that a generic freshness claim leaves unresolved.
dataNeeded: Explicit use date and necessary storage conditions
Batch expiry or merchant minimum-life commitment
Quality refunds, substitutions, complaints and completed orders
candidates.experiment: Randomize AI-origin shoppers who provide an intended use date before assignment. Compare existing accurate life labels with use-date qualification. Primary endpoint is retained, fulfilled paid baskets per eligible shopper; unsafe or false date claims are stop conditions. Enroll across multiple replenishment cycles, then complete refund observation; power depends on dated-product traffic and mismatch prevalence.
candidates.metric: Retained paid baskets per all randomized eligible AI-origin shoppers. Report use-date fulfillment accuracy, substitutions and food-quality refunds separately; do not optimize basket conversion by concealing short dates.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; ocado-fresh is an adjacent merchant benchmark, food-dates defines a constraint. Neither supplies an AI-origin uplift estimate.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown eligible N, baseline retained-basket conversion b0, remaining-life mismatch rate f and basket contribution m.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental retained baskets = N*(bT-b0). Value subtracts batch-selection, waste, substitution and fulfillment cost. The effect may be zero/negative if extra constraints narrow choice or allocation cannot honor the promise.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 400 per merchant per month, with integration priced separately and renewal tied to retained basket contribution.
candidates.costControl: Evaluate dates and batch rules deterministically. Start with a category that has reliable batch data instead of inferring expiry from product descriptions.
dependencies: Batch-aware inventory or enforceable merchant minimum-life policy
Fulfillment allocation capable of honoring the selected promise
User-supplied date and appropriate storage facts
candidates.failureMode: Batch data arrive too late, substitutions violate the promise, or a quality date is confused with a safety date.
candidates.falsifier: Merchant cannot reliably honor the use-date promise, or the test produces no net contribution after waste, refunds and allocation cost.

candidates.title: Reserve a chosen variant for the real checkout handoff
candidates.buyer: Merchants with scarce sizes, one-off products or inventory that often disappears between agent selection and payment.
candidates.problem: A conversational cart can remain available while its selected variant sells out before the buyer reaches checkout.
candidates.mechanism: Checkout completion: after the buyer explicitly selects an item, a short real inventory hold protects the handoff and reduces stock-failure abandonment. Benefits must exceed sales displaced by blocked inventory.
candidates.intervention: Add an idempotent reservation backed by the merchant's inventory system, bound to SKU, quantity, checkout and server expiry. Release on cancellation, payment or timeout; revalidate price and explain any change. Display the actual expiry without resetting it or claiming false scarcity.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify draft orders already reserve inventory, and native agent Cart MCP already persists carts. The hypothesis is applying a genuine reservation at the right handoff and proving net orders after displacement, not inventing reservations or shared carts.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A narrowly triggered, real hold increases total retained orders for high-race inventory more than it costs in blocked stock.
dataNeeded: Stock-failure events between selection and checkout
All-channel retained orders and reservation occupancy
candidates.experiment: Randomize independent merchant/warehouse inventory pools to hold-enabled or current behavior, or use preregistered switchback blocks with a washout longer than all outstanding holds and relevant browsing carryover. Shopper-level randomization alone contaminates the control through shared stock. Primary retained paid orders from AI-origin journeys per pool-period; all-channel contribution is a guardrail. Run enough pool-periods for power across demand peaks.
candidates.metric: Incremental retained AI-origin orders per randomized inventory pool-period, with total all-channel orders, margin and stock-block minutes reported. A higher held-cart conversion rate alone is insufficient.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; shopify-reserve and shopify-carts establish primitives and existing overlap. No net purchase result is documented here.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown pool-period baseline order count O0, AI handoff stock-failure rate f, hold duration and displaced demand D.
impactScenario.calculation: Net merchant value = incremental retained AI-origin contribution minus lost non-AI contribution, integration and holding cost. Zero/negative is possible even when held-cart conversion rises.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 300 per store per month; reject renewal if total merchant contribution falls despite more AI-attributed orders.
candidates.costControl: Create holds only after explicit selection and release promptly. Cap abuse and reservation occupancy using deterministic rules.
dependencies: Cluster experiment with observable all-channel displacement
candidates.failureMode: Holds become free inventory hoarding, deny stock to more committed buyers or outlive checkout failures.
candidates.falsifier: Total retained order contribution fails the break-even threshold or stock denial offsets all AI-origin gains.

candidates.title: Ask for a refill when the customer's supply will actually run out
candidates.buyer: Consumable-goods merchants with repeat purchases and dependable product quantities.
candidates.problem: A fixed postpurchase delay may prompt a refill too early or after the customer has run out and bought elsewhere.
candidates.mechanism: Repeat purchase: an opt-in, customer-correctable usage clock subtracts real delivery lead time from a declared depletion date, then offers a currently suitable reorder for approval. The proposed gain is retained repeat orders in an AI-origin acquisition cohort.
candidates.intervention: After an AI-origin purchase, offer an optional supply reminder using pack quantity, customer-entered use rate or preferred refill date and shipping time. Let customers snooze, correct or disable it; suppress after a reorder and require purchase approval. Never infer health needs or sensitive household circumstances.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Klaviyo already has replenishment flows and repurchase suppression. Its documented general expected-order model is not product-specific. Shop already reorders through agents. The difference proposed is a customer-correctable depletion date plus lead time, not reordering itself.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Explicit consumption timing improves retained repurchase versus a well-configured product-cycle replenishment flow.
dataNeeded: Product quantity and customer-entered usage/refill date
Reorders, skips, opt-outs and long-horizon retained revenue
candidates.experiment: Randomize consenting customers acquired through AI to current product-specific replenishment timing or the correctable supply clock, with equal contact budgets. Follow at least two expected consumption cycles; primary retained repeat purchase count per randomized customer. Distinguish genuinely incremental demand from purchases merely pulled forward by measuring cumulative contribution over the full horizon.
candidates.metric: Retained repeat orders per randomized customer in the preidentified AI-origin cohort. Label these as AI-origin cohort repeat revenue, not new AI-discovered orders.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; klaviyo-replenish, klaviyo-predict and shop-personal establish strong adjacent competition and scoped implementation limits.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown N opted-in AI-origin acquired customers, baseline repeat orders r0 over two cycles, average replenishment margin m and consumption-clock accuracy.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental repeat contribution = N*(rT-r0)*m minus communication/integration costs. Zero/negative remains possible; an earlier first reorder is not incremental if the longer-horizon count is unchanged.

candidates.title: Start an event offer only after its channel state is ready
candidates.buyer: Merchants running short promotions or product launches with material AI shopping traffic.
candidates.problem: A truthful sale may start and finish before an external shopping surface has processed the current offer; accepted data uploads are not proof of public availability.
candidates.mechanism: Discovery and checkout: prepare supported data early, verify actual channel state, and keep public offers and checkout consistent during the event. Recovering usable event hours could generate purchases, if propagation delay currently loses demand.
candidates.intervention: A merchant-owned release scheduler tracks intended effective time, platform submission, acceptance, observed public state and checkout truth. Preflight compliant future-event data, perform real activation/update/removal jobs at the correct time, and use channel-specific start rules. At expiry, remove the sale rather than extending a countdown.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Google already separates promotion display/effective dates and has reviews. OpenAI file-upload date fields do not themselves schedule stock changes, sale activation or removal. Native scheduling exists in parts of the stack; the proposed edge is verified cross-channel readiness and paid outcomes.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Measured readiness orchestration earns more retained AI-origin purchases across a complete event than a routine launch-day feed update.
dataNeeded: Authoritative offer and checkout effective dates
Submission/acceptance logs and observed live snapshots
Discount, margin, return and all-channel order data
candidates.experiment: Randomize comparable merchant-event clusters to standard launch operations or readiness orchestration, stratified by event type and planned demand. Count retained AI-origin orders across the full event plus an equal postevent window. Use many independent events rather than one before/after sale; power includes cluster correlation. Concurrent discounts, ad spend and promotion terms must match.
candidates.metric: Retained AI-origin orders and contribution per randomized merchant-event, using fixed event windows. Report surface visibility only as a mediator; all-channel contribution catches channel displacement.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; google-promo, google-display, google-recrawl and openai-dates document real asynchronous boundaries. No propagation-to-purchase elasticity is assumed.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown per-event baseline retained orders O0, demand during delayed hours H, current propagation distribution and margin after discount m.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental contribution = randomized event order difference*m minus scheduling/monitoring cost. A recovered hour has no assumed conversion value; effects may be zero or negative if the event demand window shifts or discount costs dominate.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 500 per merchant per event for a managed pilot; recurring pricing requires reproducible contribution over several events.
candidates.costControl: Use platform events/status APIs where available and bounded public sampling near real transitions. Do not repeatedly request recrawls as an acceleration tactic.

Approved channel access and supported lifecycle operations
Enough independent events for a credible comparison
candidates.failureMode: Platform lag is uncontrollable, samples misrepresent shopper visibility, or delaying a launch sacrifices more demand than it recovers.
candidates.falsifier: Orchestration changes logs but not usable live offer time, or retained event contribution fails to improve after full-window follow-up.

candidates.title: Spend catalog repair capacity before the category's buying window
candidates.buyer: Large seasonal merchants or feed agencies with more fixable defects than their weekly work budget permits.
candidates.problem: Uniform catalog refreshes can repair a low-demand category while a time-sensitive category still contains a purchase-blocking defect.
candidates.mechanism: Enabling allocation: move an unchanged repair budget toward verified conversion blockers before the expected buying window, allowing those fixes to affect more real AI-origin purchase opportunities. A demand forecast alone creates no conversion value.
candidates.intervention: A scheduler ranks verified defects by upcoming eligible demand, observed causal repair value, repair lead time and channel propagation delay. Compare with the merchant's current queue; preserve a minimum service level for low-volume items and exploration for uncertain categories. Do not treat Google category interest as all-AI demand.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Google Merchant Center already provides popular-product/assortment insights and Google Ads category search interest; feed tools already prioritize work. The proposed edge is choosing repair timing under a fixed budget using purchase evidence and delayed propagation.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A purchase-evidence-informed repair schedule creates more retained AI-origin orders than the current queue with the same engineering hours and compute.
dataNeeded: Time-stamped verified defects and repair effort
Seasonal first-party purchase demand and AI-origin cohort data
Prior randomized repair effects with uncertainty
Google category signals as optional proxies
candidates.experiment: Randomize comparable merchant or independent category clusters to the existing queue or the timing scheduler with identical weekly labor/compute budgets. Evaluate fixed full-season retained AI-origin order counts and total contribution, including postpeak follow-up. Require sufficient clusters and baseline balance; model contamination from substitute products. No assumed power from repeated synthetic shoppers.
candidates.metric: Incremental retained AI-origin orders per fixed budget per randomized cluster-season. Cost per incremental retained order is secondary and undefined when the causal gain is zero or negative.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized allocation benefit; google-demand, google-popular and google-recrawl support inputs and timing constraints. No source proves this scheduler's conversion gain.

impactScenario.baseline: Unknown fixed repair budget B, control orders O0, upcoming eligible demand D, verified blocker prevalence f and causal value of each repair. No uplift prior is asserted.
impactScenario.calculation: Compare O_scheduler - O_current over the same fixed budget and season. Contribution difference must exceed software/integration cost. Better forecast accuracy or lower model cost alone does not satisfy the claim; zero/negative purchase difference remains possible.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 600 per merchant per month for a high-volume pilot, contingent on incremental contribution at unchanged repair resources.
candidates.costControl: This is the cost-allocation idea: reuse cheap deterministic defect checks and invoke expensive analysis where a repair can plausibly affect upcoming orders. Do not reduce fulfillment or policy accuracy for low-volume items.
dependencies: A backlog of verified, fixable purchase blockers
Historical or fresh randomized repair evidence
candidates.failureMode: The forecast chases noise, seasonal demand changes faster than propagation, or the prioritized defects have no causal effect on purchases.
candidates.falsifier: At the same total work budget, the scheduler fails to increase retained contribution versus the existing queue over a full preregistered season.

candidates.title: Repair cross-channel product identity collisions before checkout
candidates.buyer: Multi-brand retailers whose AI referrals span merchant SKUs, global identifiers and regional variants.
candidates.problem: An AI agent can identify the intended product family but resolve a different edition, pack size or regional variant when it follows an offer into checkout. Actual prevalence must be audited.
candidates.mechanism: Selection-to-cart: preserve the exact trade item across discovery and handoff, preventing an apparent match from becoming a wrong-item landing or abandoned cart. Product identity is separate from seller and shopper identity.
candidates.intervention: Create a contradiction-aware crosswalk among manufacturer model/GTIN, merchant variant ID and offer ID. A resolver returns an exact match only when region, edition and pack quantity agree; otherwise it requests one discriminating choice. Test the ID chain at search, product, cart and order boundaries.
candidates.competitorOverlap: OpenAI already models product/variant/offer identifiers; GS1 already verifies identifier ownership. Generic catalog mapping overlaps. The remaining hypothesis is cross-channel contradiction detection and repair, not generating more identifiers.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: A focused resolver can rescue observed wrong-variant handoffs that clean feeds and native variant grouping still leave unresolved.
dataNeeded: Manufacturer model/GTIN evidence including edition, region and pack quantity
Consented or non-personal transaction lineage for comparing selected and ordered items
candidates.experiment: First replay known ID collisions and honest unknowns offline. Then randomize eligible users of a merchant-owned AI shopping flow to the existing resolver or the contradiction-aware resolver, keeping factual inventory/prices equal. Primary endpoint is paid, non-cancelled purchases retained at 30 days. Plan 6 to 8 weeks of enrollment, extend only under a pre-set power rule; protect latency and wrong-item returns. External engine monitoring is a separate transfer check.
candidates.metric: Retained purchases per all randomized eligible shoppers, with one stable first-party assignment per shopper where consent permits; otherwise session-level inference is labelled. Count all merchant purchases to detect SKU substitution, and separately report exact-item success.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase effect. openai-feed and gs1 establish available identity mechanisms, not lift.

impactScenario.baseline: No traffic, conversion or fault-prevalence baseline has been measured. N is the number of eligible AI shopping entrants; pC and pT are randomized retained-purchase probabilities.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental retained purchases = N * (pT - pC). Break-even requires N * (pT - pC) * g > GBP 400 + V, where g is contribution per incremental retained purchase and V is incremental verification, integration amortization and operating cost. Fee is an unvalidated test price; no uplift assumption is supplied.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based test: GBP 400 per merchant per month after an observed collision audit; charge only if retained contribution can plausibly cover the fee.
candidates.costControl: Use deterministic key checks first, cache manufacturer mappings by version and send only genuine contradictions for manual review.
dependencies: A controlled AI entry point or deployable merchant handoff adapter
candidates.failureMode: Over-conservative matching removes legitimate offers or adds clarification friction; false confidence sends shoppers to the wrong product.
candidates.falsifier: A sampled audit finds negligible resolvable identity errors, or a powered trial excludes the merchant's break-even retained-purchase effect.

candidates.title: Keep each cart line attached to its actual wearer
candidates.buyer: Apparel and uniform merchants serving shoppers who buy for several consenting adults in one cart.
candidates.problem: A signed-in buyer is not necessarily the person wearing every garment. Account-level fit context can contaminate a mixed-person basket; whether a given fit provider already solves this must be checked.
candidates.mechanism: Sizing-to-purchase: resolving wearer identity for each line prevents a confident recommendation for the wrong person, increasing purchases that survive the return window.
candidates.intervention: Add a wearer selector with explicit permission for each invited adult. Bind an opaque wearer reference, provider recommendation and product version to each cart line; recompute only the affected line when the wearer changes. Keep raw measurements inside the selected provider and do not overwrite the purchaser's default profile.

candidates.metric: Retained orders per randomized multi-wearer group, with line-level wrong-wearer recommendations as a diagnostic. Do not compare voluntary fit users with non-users as if randomized.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized for this specific identity defect. truefit-spec describes adjacent capabilities and vendor outcomes; none establish the incremental effect of line-to-wearer binding.

Manufacturer compatibility matrix with revision coverage

candidates.problem: The public price can fail a shopper's stated budget before the shopper reaches an existing eligibility offer. Verification and coupon activation can also become disconnected from the chosen cart.

Paid orders, discount cost and contribution

candidates.title: Resolve a household veto before generating the final shortlist

candidates.problem: A single shopper's AI conversation may omit a consenting co-buyer whose dimensions, budget or material requirements later rule out the shortlist. Shared browsing history is not permission to infer a household.
candidates.mechanism: Shortlist-to-purchase: explicitly collecting each participant's required constraints reduces late rejection and repeated search, allowing the group to choose a purchase that all decision-makers accept.
candidates.intervention: Create a voluntary, task-limited buying project. Each invited adult supplies chosen constraints and decides what other participants can see. candidates.edgeHypothesis: For purchases with a real second decision-maker, surfacing a concrete conflicting constraint before the shortlist beats passing links between people after selection.

candidates.title: Use recipient-approved substitutions when a gift-list item is unavailable
candidates.buyer: Gift and registry merchants whose AI shopping visitors encounter unavailable or unsuitable listed items.
candidates.problem: A wish-list item can be unavailable, while the buyer lacks permission or enough context to choose a substitute. Inferring the recipient's interests from public profiles would be a poor substitute for explicit preference sharing.
candidates.mechanism: Unavailable selection-to-purchase: a recipient-approved alternative policy lets a giver find an acceptable in-stock gift without exposing private recipient data or abandoning the task.
candidates.intervention: Let an adult recipient opt into a limited substitution policy for a list item, such as approved product families, colors, maximum duplicates and forbidden alternatives. A permissioned resolver returns only acceptable available choices. Use reservation expiry and merchant-confirmed purchase events to prevent duplicate gifts; keep delivery information with the merchant.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Giftster already has group visibility and reservation/purchased states. A basic private wishlist is not new. This idea tests recipient-authorized substitute selection and reliable completed-purchase reconciliation; a public Giftster API or missing feature is not assumed.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: When the exact listed item fails, a bounded recipient-approved alternative can convert a stalled gift session more reliably than a generic recommendation or asking the recipient again.
candidates.experiment: Randomize at gift occasion/list cluster after a genuine unavailable-item trigger, comparing existing wishlist fallback with the approved-substitution flow. Keep the original recipient requirements equally visible where permission allows. Primary endpoint is a paid gift order retained at 30 days; duplicate purchases and recipient rejection are guardrails. Plan 8 to 12 weeks across enough independent occasions, account for seasonality and avoid mixing treatment within one list.
candidates.metric: Retained gift purchases per randomized failed-item occasion, plus total occasion spending and duplication. Reservation clicks are not purchases and fewer duplicate purchases can lower gross orders while improving retained value.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. giftster-sharing establishes existing list-sharing and reservation workflows, not this substitution mechanism's purchase effect.

impactScenario.calculation: Incremental retained purchases = N * (pT - pC). Break-even requires N * (pT - pC) * g > GBP 400 + V, where g is contribution per incremental retained purchase and V is incremental verification, integration amortization and operating cost. Fee is an unvalidated test price; no uplift assumption is supplied.

candidates.costControl: Evaluate simple approved substitution rules before using a model, cache public product equivalence, and release stale reservations deterministically.
dependencies: Recipient opt-in before the unavailable-item event
Registry/merchant partnership or a first-party registry
Private fulfillment handoff supported by the merchant
candidates.failureMode: The substitute is technically allowed but unwanted; stale reservations suppress good purchases; permissions reveal recipient information to the giver.

candidates.title: Recover verified shopping agents blocked between discovery and cart
candidates.buyer: Merchants whose permitted AI shopping agents encounter documented false bot blocks or challenges.
candidates.problem: An agent may authenticate successfully at one commerce endpoint and lose the recognized identity path at a redirect, proxy or protected cart endpoint. A signed agent is not automatically a user-authorized purchaser.
candidates.mechanism: Access-to-purchase: repair a proven identity-verification interruption for permitted shopping actions so legitimate purchase intent can reach a valid cart, while leaving consumer authorization and payment checks intact.
candidates.intervention: Trace an approved agent through merchant-controlled entry, redirect and cart endpoints using test identities. Locate where trusted signature verification or recognized endpoint routing fails; implement the vendor-supported configuration repair. If trust cannot be established, offer a normal human continuation with selected items. Never whitelist by user-agent text or bypass a legitimate denial.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol and Cloudflare already provide signed-agent recognition. The remaining product is fault-specific diagnosis and conversion validation across a merchant's actual integration, not an invented agent identity standard.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Merchants with verified false blocks can recover retained orders through narrow supported configuration fixes without increasing abuse losses.
dataNeeded: Merchant-authorized endpoint and edge logs with secrets removed
Approved agent key/issuer and verification status
Explicit shopper action/session authorization where required
Purchase outcomes, fraud losses and server load
candidates.experiment: Replay known authorized and denied cases in a merchant-controlled environment. Then randomize verified, policy-eligible agent shopping sessions between the existing safe fallback and the repaired route. Primary endpoint is paid orders retained at 30 days; fraud, chargebacks, denied-request acceptance and resource abuse are hard guardrails. Plan 6 to 10 weeks, with power based on natural false-block traffic. Do not manufacture or probe failures on third-party systems.
candidates.metric: Retained orders per randomized verified eligible shopping session, with effects weighted by the independently measured natural block prevalence for an all-traffic estimate. A fall in challenge rate alone is not conversion lift.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized incremental effect. visa-tap and cloudflare-agents establish recognition mechanisms and existing competition, not the prevalence or revenue cost of any merchant's false blocks.

impactScenario.baseline: No traffic, conversion or fault-prevalence baseline has been measured. N is the number of eligible naturally affected policy-eligible agent shopping sessions; pC and pT are randomized retained-purchase probabilities.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental retained purchases = N * (pT - pC). Break-even requires N * (pT - pC) * g > GBP 1000 + V, where g is contribution per incremental retained purchase and V is incremental verification, integration amortization and operating cost. Fee is an unvalidated test price; no uplift assumption is supplied.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test: GBP 1000 per month for a merchant with enough verified lost purchases; compare against its existing edge vendor's included troubleshooting.
candidates.costControl: Fix repeatable configuration faults rather than buying repeated simulated purchases; use sampled request traces and deterministic verification diagnostics.
dependencies: Merchant control over its edge and commerce endpoints
No relaxation of shopper consent or payment authority
candidates.failureMode: The alleged block is intentional policy, the fix admits abuse, or traffic is too small to justify a separate product.
candidates.falsifier: No reproducible permitted identity interruption exists, the edge vendor fixes it within current support, or incremental retained contribution is erased by abuse and operating cost.

candidates.title: Admit a simulator only after it predicts purchase-winning interventions
candidates.buyer: An ecommerce experimentation lead deciding which AI discovery fixes deserve scarce live traffic.
candidates.problem: A larger simulated recommendation delta can select the wrong patch because model preferences, retrieval context and human purchases differ.
candidates.mechanism: Across discovery and checkout, a calibrated ranking of candidate interventions could put useful changes into live tests earlier. Orders rise only if this changes the chosen releases or their timing enough to beat the current selection process.
candidates.intervention: Create a paired intervention registry containing frozen simulator effects and independently randomized merchant purchase effects. Train a hierarchical predictor of treatment ranking, not an absolute ChatGPT conversion rate. Hold out merchants, intervention families and future periods; abstain for unsupported contexts. Estimate prediction uncertainty including noisy trial estimates.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Shopify SimGym already offers synthetic theme comparisons and Shopify Rollouts offers live experiments; Lily Max advertises a test-and-deploy loop. The proposed distinction is prospectively demonstrated purchase-valued selection quality, not adding simulation to A/B testing. Undocumented calibration in competitors remains unknown.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: Simulator evidence adds predictive value beyond pre-period traffic, defect type and an experienced operator, and a calibrated selector earns more orders at the same live-test budget.
dataNeeded: Frozen simulator inputs, model versions and within-intent reruns
Unselected as well as selected candidate interventions
Independent live randomization and paid-order outcomes
Baseline merchant, product category, actual engine, country and task mix
Separate training and prospective evaluation cohorts
candidates.experiment: Randomize sufficiently independent merchant portfolios to calibrated selection or the existing selection workflow for a fixed release budget. Each arm still validates candidate patches in live randomized trials. Primary endpoint is cumulative verified AI-origin paid orders per preassigned portfolio over a fixed horizon, with all-channel orders and margin guardrails. Use at least a complete deployment, indexing and purchase cycle; power the policy comparison at portfolio level. Include a random exploration sample of candidates to avoid learning only from historical winners.
candidates.metric: Intention-to-treat difference in AI-origin paid-order counts per randomized portfolio, baseline-adjusted using only pre-treatment data. Attribution coverage is reported; unknown-origin orders are separate. Cross-validated ranking accuracy is diagnostic, not conversion lift. Reruns estimate model noise, not human sample size.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase impact. transport states why transfer needs explicit assumptions; llm-diversity gives adjacent evidence against treating model reruns as a human population. Neither supplies a shopping lift percentage.

impactScenario.baseline: No merchant baseline supplied. Let V be fixed-horizon eligible demand and d be the difference in true purchase effect of patches selected by the two policies.
impactScenario.calculation: Incremental orders = V*d, minus any extra order loss caused by the calibration policy's exploration or deployment delay, if not already included in d.
impactScenario.range: Unknown; zero if both policies choose the same useful releases, negative if calibration is wrong or slows release.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based pilot: GBP 1,000 per portfolio per month, only worth testing where measured incremental contribution can exceed the fee and extra experimentation cost.
candidates.costControl: Use small paired simulator batches for within-intent uncertainty; spend additional calls on new independent tasks only when they can change selection.
dependencies: Several real intervention trials, including nulls and harms
Permission to retain de-identified experiment summaries
Sufficient independent portfolios for a policy trial
candidates.failureMode: Calibration overfits a few successful merchants or an old engine version; a good proxy prediction hides a poor absolute purchase decision.
candidates.falsifier: On unseen merchants and future periods, the calibrated policy fails to beat operator or uncalibrated selection on cumulative purchases within the same cost and risk budget.

candidates.title: Plan catalogue trials around propagation and stable assignment
candidates.buyer: A merchant or agency testing factual product-source changes that external engines crawl or ingest asynchronously.
candidates.problem: An ordinary session A/B test cannot give a global external crawler two stable versions of one source. Rapid alternation and early readouts can mix cached treatments and produce false deployment decisions.
candidates.mechanism: Discovery-stage trials that survive real ingestion lag can identify effective source repairs and avoid discarding slow genuine gains or rolling out cache artifacts. The conversion benefit depends on which deployment decisions this changes.
candidates.intervention: Build a design compiler that groups variant families, canonical duplicates and tightly linked pages into persistent randomized clusters; blocks on pre-period demand; and chooses a fixed observation horizon from propagation pilots. Keep assignment stable throughout. Use received, published and externally observed versions as diagnostics, never as a post-treatment filter for the primary sample.
candidates.competitorOverlap: Statsig already documents canonical-URL SEO trials, indexing lag and cannibalization guardrails; DataFeedWatch already has product-title A/B workflows. The edge must be supported treatment-family clustering, actual source propagation evidence and purchase-valued decisions beyond those tools.
candidates.edgeHypothesis: For persistent source changes, stable family-level designs reduce decision errors enough to generate more orders than independent URL or alternating-title tests.
dataNeeded: Pre-period order counts, demand and seasonality
Source version publication times and observable fetch/ingestion evidence
Paid orders linked to eligible product families and reliable AI-origin evidence
candidates.experiment: Randomize disjoint product-family clusters to an actionable truthful source repair or unchanged source, with inference at cluster level. The primary analysis includes every assigned cluster from the predeclared start; do not reset the clock only for treated pages observed by a crawler. Evaluate the compiler against the current design workflow across independent portfolios, measuring subsequent purchase outcomes of their chosen releases. Plan duration from carryover and order delay, and power from cluster count and intracluster correlation; short switchbacks are disallowed when carryover is unbounded.
candidates.metric: Verified AI-origin paid orders per fixed assigned cluster-week; total merchant orders and substitute-family orders are guardrails. Conversion per arriving AI session is secondary because the repair can change who arrives. Count all eligible units, including unpropagated treatments.
candidates.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase improvement. statsig-seo proves workflow overlap; switchback-paper explains the importance of carryover assumptions, not an expected AI shopping benefit.

impactScenario.baseline: No measured propagation delays or order effect supplied. Let L be orders lost by wrong release decisions under the current design and R be extra orders lost through longer correct trials.
impactScenario.calculation: Decision-policy incremental orders = avoided L - additional R over the same fixed horizon.
impactScenario.range: May be zero or negative when current designs are already adequate, clusters are too few, or waiting costs exceed avoided errors.

candidates.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated test price: GBP 500 per multi-category trial, subject to an incremental contribution break-even calculation using the merchant's own margin.
candidates.costControl: Reuse existing experiment assignment and warehouse systems; audit representative version propagation instead of issuing redundant model calls.
candidates.failureMode: Cross-family substitution or engine-wide re-ranking still contaminates clusters; a longer trial loses the entire selling season.
candidates.falsifier: Against the existing URL-based workflow, the design changes few decisions or produces no gain in purchases after accounting for its longer test duration.
